stories.Headline: Kai McPheeters bids $10 million for Character.ai platform as Common Sense Media urges judge to protect children's chats
stories.Summary:
A $10 million offer to buy Character Technologies Inc.'s AI chatbot platform came from Smirks & Pangs Acquisition LLC, whose authorized signatory is Kai McPheeters, a 29-year-old gamer, according to a Monday filing in the US Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware. The bid was tapped as the minimum starting bid for Character.ai's consumer-facing platform, accounts and chat content, brand, and deep learning architectures. Common Sense Media asked the judge overseeing the bankruptcy to protect user conversations in any sale, in a letter dated November 12, 2026. The clerk of the US Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware stamped the letter received at 9:59 a.m. on November 13. It was filed as Docket No. 167 in case 26-11603 and appeared on the public docket on November 16.

The letter asks the court to ensure any sale includes robust privacy protections for all conversational data, a commitment to a comprehensive privacy program, and effective age-assurance measures. It requests that the court take into account promises made to children by Character.AI and that any sale address strong privacy protections for children's and all conversational chatbot data, a strong privacy program, and adequate age assurance. The six-page letter is addressed to Judge Brendan L. Shannon, who presides over the case, and was shipped by FedEx from the group's Washington, DC office on November 12. The filing runs to 84 pages with two attached AI risk assessments, both rating Character.ai "Unacceptable" for anyone under 18 and both last updated April 10, 2025. One assessment covers Character.ai alone, the other covers Social AI Companions including Character.AI, Nomi and Replika.

The letter is signed by Amina Fazlullah, Head of Tech Policy Advocacy, Ariel Fox Johnson, Senior Advisor for Data Privacy, and Brenna Leasor, Tech Policy Advisor. It argues that removing names from chat logs would not protect children because AI "may allow purchasers or third parties to identify children or infer sensitive information from their conversations." Footnote 13 says all conversational data is deserving of protection in the sale and that it is not clear whether age assurance mechanisms were always or ever effective, so children's data may not be appropriately classified as such. The letter does not describe itself as an objection and does not cite a section of the Bankruptcy Code. It was mailed to the judge rather than filed electronically through counsel, and the docket lists it as a response.

The letter says that even if personal identifiers like names are removed, conversations alone could reveal who children are, and that conversational snippets could be analyzed by AI in ways that expose children, including sensitive inferences. It quotes privacy law scholar Daniel J. Solove's paper dated October 19, 2026, saying AI's power to generate inferences from data creates an enormous problem for privacy law. It warns the chats could be used to target children known to have proclivities for gambling, to charge children higher rates, or by criminal actors to sextort or blackmail children, and could be sold to data brokers and become part of a digital dossier following the child through credit, jobs and education. It cites the FTC's action over 25 years ago against ToySmart, a children's toy e-retailer that went bankrupt and attempted to sell data including children's names, birthdays and addresses at auction, citing the FTC's settlement announcement of July 21, 2000. It says children did not understand their data would be sold, and that testing showed Character.ai reassured children their conversations were confidential, quoting one chatbot: "Anything you share here stays just between you and me. That's a promise."

According to the letter, users under 13 were technically restricted to comply with federal privacy laws, but age determination relied on self-attestation, likely enabling children to regularly access the platform, and users under 18 could use the service during assessments and up until November 25, 202 with the final digit of the year missing in the filed copy. The chief executive's first-day declaration says Character spent several months beginning in October 2025 restricting users under 18 from open-ended chats and eventually eliminated that access. On October 14, 39 states and the District of Columbia said minors had used the platform without adequate age checks and that their data was likely recorded as adult data, asking for age assurance not relying only on self-declared birthdates. The Kentucky complaint cited by the states put US accounts at more than 21.6 million by March 13, 2025, of which more than 2.1 million declared an age under 18. In voice mode, testers found conversations that seemed entirely without the guardrails on teen accounts, and these speech exchanges were captured in text transcription in the chat window and saved with all the text chats.

Appendix A says Character.AI companions are intended to be your companion, so the information they have about you is inherently personal and incredibly risky. It describes a December 2024 incident, quoting the company that during an attempt to refresh the list of featured Characters on the homepage it mistakenly triggered a change that temporarily made parts of users' account pages publicly visible, possibly including username, name, bio, Characters, homepage, personas, voices or chats. The assessment adds that estimates suggest tens of thousands of users could have had their info viewable to anyone online at the time. It also notes that at least one hack of a socia, with the article ending there. The letter's pricing point is footnoted to a Common Sense Media explainer, "AdTech and Kids: Behavioral Ads Need a Time-Out," and the blackmail point to a 2019 Common Sense Media paper, "Privacy Risks and Harms."

Judge Brendan Linehan Shannon held a hearing Tuesday and approved the consumer privacy ombudsman procedures pitched by Character.ai. The letter does not propose specific terms, and the judge decides what any sale order will contain. The letter does not say which test account received the chatbot's confidential reply, when, or whether it came from a company-built character or a user-created one. On Character.ai anyone can create a character, and the attached assessment says the company's own models power the conversations. The articles leave open what the sale order will contain and how the missing final digit of the year in the filed copy should read.

stories.Headline: Bharat Semi raises $24 million to develop AI enabled image sensors
stories.Summary:
The New Delhi startup Bharat Semi raised 24 million dollars in seed funding to develop AI enabled image sensors. This all equity funding round occurred in November 2026 to support product development and global market expansion. The company intends to use this capital to expand its engineering team and prepare for commercial production. It has already secured design wins with General Atomics and Kaynes Semicon, though sensors are still under development. The startup aims to begin its initial commercial production of these programmable image sensors during the year 2027.

The technology integrates image capture, processing, and AI on one chip to reduce system costs by at least 70 percent. Funding was led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons, and Indus Bridge Ventures, with Valour Capital and Micromax participating. Gaingels and individual investors also joined the round to help the company target customers in the United States. The startup currently employs 75 people across India and Santa Clara, California, and is hiring engineers in Europe. It plans to increase its American workforce to around 20 employees by the middle of the year 2027.

Co founder Vrinda Kapoor stated that the company aims to move from simple sensors to complete sense making solutions. She explained that the new architecture eliminates the need for separate processing components used in conventional vision system setups. Kapoor noted that the latest funding will not be used to finance the proposed separate semiconductor fabrication facility. She mentioned that the company will follow a fabless model by outsourcing manufacturing to focus on design and software. The startup is working to identify domestic partners to build and operate the proposed Indian fabrication facility.

The technology targets applications in aerospace, surveillance, industrial automation, and smart homes to provide advanced automated sensing capabilities. Air conditioners could use these sensors to detect room occupancy, while drones could process visual information without extra hardware. The company is affected by the AI boom, which allows Indian startups to develop specialized chips for global markets. India is attempting to become an alternative manufacturing hub as American companies look to diversify supply chains beyond China. This effort is supported by the India Semiconductor Mission 2.0, which has a budget of 1,27,500 crore rupees.

Bharat Semi was founded in late 2021 by Vrinda Kapoor, a South Park Commons fellow, and managing director Vinayak Dalmia. Dalmia previously worked in private equity and at McKinsey, while chief technology officer Boyd Fowler came from OmniVision. The company is currently pre revenue and has already developed prototypes for its first generation of image sensors. In 2024, the startup announced a semiconductor fabrication project in India through a partnership with the US Space Force. This fabrication initiative remains under development and is separate from the current image sensor business and seed funding.

First generation sensors are in prototyping, while second generation sensors with advanced AI should reach prototyping by mid 2027. The company expects to deliver these newer sensors to its customers by the end of the year 2027. The articles leave open whether the startup will successfully identify the domestic partners needed for its fabrication project. It remains unclear if the company can establish itself as a major player in the global chip manufacturing hub. The reports do not state when the partnership with the US Space Force will reach a final conclusion.

stories.Headline: Apple splits device control into app and folder permissions in macOS 27.3 beta to curb AI agent risks
stories.Summary:
Apple released the macOS 27.3 beta on November 16, 2026, to provide Mac users with more control over their shared data. This update introduces new privacy controls for apps that use AI agents to access system functions. The company is changing how users grant permissions for device control and full disk access. These updates aim to protect users from risks associated with the growing popularity of AI apps. The changes are part of a broader effort to increase transparency for Mac users.

The Device Control and Data Access setting is now split into System & App Protection Override and Accessibility. Users will grant permissions by selecting a requesting app from a list instead of using a single method. Apple encourages granting access only to specific folders for Full Disk Access or specific apps for the override. A blue transparency indicator will appear in the Mac menu bar when an app controls another app. Users can now configure apps to ask for required access each time instead of granting unrestricted access.

Apple informed developers that they must adjust user onboarding to ensure apps handle limited folder or app access gracefully. The company stated that these changes better inform users about the data apps will receive or control. Apple warned that some developers use Full Disk Access in ways that put users at risk. This risk includes exposing browsing history, messages, mail, and files to unauthorized AI agents. The company believes these new controls are necessary to mitigate these specific security threats.

Some users believe Apple is correctly raising awareness about the dangers of allowing AI to infiltrate a Mac. One user noted that the blue transparency indicator looks atrocious on the new PROLED MBP dynamic island. This person claimed that the new prompt replaces the old Accessibility Permissions and requires admin passwords or Touch ID. Other users expressed frustration that they must download gigabytes of software even if they have no interest in AI. These changes affect any app that previously required accessibility permissions, not just those using AI.

Apple stated last month that additional controls for Full Disk Access were needed because of risks from AI agents. Current known apps keep their existing experience without an entitlement, and permissions granted before macOS 27.3 remain in effect. Apps for assistive technologies or disk backup can request entitlements to maintain their previous installation experience. The company is responding to a trend where AI agents require deep system access to function. These measures are designed to prevent the accidental exposure of sensitive personal user data.

Mac users will see these new privacy changes when they approve new app permission requests. Apple has stated that further details regarding entitlements for developers are coming soon. The articles do not specify the exact date when the final version of macOS 27.3 will launch. It remains unclear if the entitlement process will work for apps that are not in the App Store. The text leaves open whether users can permanently acknowledge an app to remove the menu bar indicator.

stories.Headline: China and ASEAN designate 2027 as the Year of AI cooperation
stories.Summary:
China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations declared 2027 as the Year of AI cooperation on Monday, November 16, 2026. This announcement took place during the 29th China-ASEAN Summit held in Manila to foster regional technological growth. The agreement establishes a formal timeline for the two parties to collaborate on artificial intelligence initiatives. This partnership aims to integrate advanced computing tools across various sectors within the member nations.

The initiative requires the implementation of AI plus cooperation to create a powerful engine for high-quality economic development across the region. This follows China's own domestic AI Plus initiative launched in 2024 to develop industry-specific tools for ports, mining, and logistics. Current data from October shows that over one-third of larger Chinese manufacturing enterprises have already adopted AI in key scenarios. Some manufacturers reported production efficiency gains between 20 and 30 percent according to a September study by the International Labour Organization.

Chinese Premier Li Qiang expressed that China is ready to work with ASEAN to ensure the success of the designated cooperation year. He stated that China is willing to pursue these joint efforts to strengthen the regional economy through technological integration. Miao Yanliang, the chief economist at China International Capital Corporation, noted that China's comprehensive industrial base and vast market provide a competitive edge. He believes these engineering capabilities will be beneficial as artificial intelligence is directed toward wider practical applications.

The broader context includes successful AI deployments in China, such as the system at Qingdao Ruilijie Metal Co., Ltd. that saves over 3 million yuan annually. Other applications include drone inspections for the State Grid Tai'an power supply company and pathology analysis at the First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University. Developers of the Qingdao moldmaking model hope to expand their reach to 100 small and medium firms by the end of the year. These domestic successes serve as a foundation for the upcoming international cooperation scheduled for 2027.

stories.Headline: Hackers use Artex AI framework to breach Barracuda and other global organizations
stories.Summary:
Barracuda suffered a cyberattack between November 1 and November 2, 2026, using the Artex agentic AI penetration testing framework. Hackers used an exposed valid cloud access key to enter the system and exfiltrate credentials from ten cloud accounts. This intrusion occurred within 44 hours and involved searching servers for seed phrase files, Ethereum keystore files, and extended private keys. The attack was carried out by financially motivated criminals who found an unrevoked credential belonging to a former third party vendor. Barracuda changed all customer credentials because its logs were not detailed enough to rule out unauthorized access to customer systems.

The Artex framework, written in Go, integrates with LLMs like OpenAI GPT, Anthropic Claude, DeepSeek, GLM, Grok, and Kimi. It was released on GitHub in July 2026 by Autumn-27 and removed on October 8, though Artex Pro exists. The tool uses a planner and AI agents to perform reconnaissance, exploit systems, escalate privileges, and steal data autonomously. Some intrusions progressed from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours, significantly reducing the time to chain techniques. The FBI released a 13-page FLASH advisory on Friday detailing how multiple threat actors have weaponized this open-source framework.

The FBI warned that Artex allows actors with minimal technical expertise to execute complex, multi-target operations simultaneously and at scale. Barracuda chief information security officer Arve Kjoelen stated that defenders relying on spotting activity often arrive after the attacker finishes. Miggo Security CEO Daniel Shechter said autonomous attackers can adapt faster than defenders can triage alerts, increasing the overall attack velocity. Amazon stated that basic security hygiene, such as addressing default credentials and unpatched software, remains the most effective defense available. The FBI urged organizations to monitor for unusual bursts of automated requests, suspicious cloud activity, and unexpected credential changes.

The ConnectWise supply-chain breach affected Microsoft 365 customer environments, with Huntress identifying 162 compromised tenants and 2,250 downstream targets. South Korean financial institutions, including Hana Bank, KB Kookmin Bank, and Shinhan Bank, saw personal data of 68,000 people stolen. South Korean police arrested seven suspects who stole 8.2 million records from educational institutions and hospitals across more than 90 organizations. Vapor Panda targeted over 200 organizations in 14 countries, including US defense, nuclear, semiconductor, pharmaceutical organizations, and a European presidency. Other affected industries include law firms, government, tech, and phone and internet companies, as noted in the FBI advisory.

Artex was first published in July 2026 and has been used in real-world attacks by Chinese actors since August. Microsoft attributed the ConnectWise campaign to the China-state-aligned group Storm-0940, while Cisco's Talos observed the financially motivated group Storm-3358 using it. Vapor Panda used the tool in October, and Barracuda noted similarities between its breach and an October Railway platform intrusion. Researchers recently found hundreds of publicly exposed Artex systems online without passwords, including the system used to target South Korea. The framework is particularly effective at identifying vulnerabilities in legacy services and partner portals that are often overlooked by defenders.

Organizations are encouraged to report suspicious activity to the FBI or its Internet Crime Complaint Center to help track threats. MalwareMustDie released an open-source detection signature pack on Friday containing rules and indicators for various security monitoring and threat tools. Companies are urged to restrict access to cloud administration interfaces, review authentication logs, and implement rate limits on sensitive APIs. The FBI cautioned that IP addresses listed in the indicators of compromise may have changed since the attacks occurred. The articles leave open exactly how many Barracuda customers were affected and whether ConnectWise will comment on the FBI claims.

stories.Headline: Liquid C2 and Graphiant launch quantum secure networking for African enterprises
stories.Summary:
Bas Wijne, the CEO of APO Group, released a report on November 16, 2026, regarding artificial intelligence research in African markets. He used data from Africa Newsroom to highlight what researchers in Europe and the United States often miss about AI assistants. The report was issued from Johannesburg, South Africa, just before the start of the Africa Tech Festival 2026. Simultaneously, Liquid C2 and Graphiant partnered to launch a Quantum Secure Network-as-a-Service to protect African enterprises from future threats. This new security offering combines post-quantum cryptography with secure AI connectivity and data sovereignty controls to safeguard sensitive corporate data.

The Reuters Institute 2023 count of news sites blocking AI covered ten countries, but none of those countries were in Africa. Africa Newsroom reaches over 250 news sites, and AI crawlers visit the platform approximately 200,000 times every single day. Microsoft Copilot cites Africa Newsroom 16,000 times monthly, while Google AI draws about 62,000 impressions from the site each month. In South Africa, 30 percent of 263 news sites block crawlers, but only 12 to 14 percent do in Senegal. Other specific markets mentioned include Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, Côte d’Ivoire, and the city of Abidjan, where procurement leads use AI assistants.

Bas Wijne stated that a company's first impression in Africa depends on which local websites AI assistants are allowed to read. He explained that generative engine optimisation helps companies be found and credited by assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and DeepSeek. Vinay Hiralall of Liquid C2 said businesses must build cybersecurity into their foundations to leverage cloud and connected operations. Ali Shaikh, CEO at Graphiant, noted that Google set 2029 as a deadline to become quantum-safe from quantum attacks. He argued that updating thousands of applications is unrealistic, so adding protection to the network covers all of them.

The report notes that 79 percent of the biggest news sites in the UK and US block at least one crawler. This affects companies trying to be found, as their announcements must exist online to be discovered by potential new customers. Meta AI inside WhatsApp is a common tool used by customers in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, and also in South Africa. African news publishers face a challenge because AI assistants use their journalism, which leads to fewer readers visiting primary sources. The new quantum service helps African enterprises maintain audit trails and simplify management while protecting data from current and future threats.

APO Group was founded in 2007 by Nicolas Pompigne-Mognard and provides visibility across all 54 African markets for its various clients. Its clients include the African Development Bank Group, Africa CDC, Afreximbank, NFL, Nestlé, Emirates, Canon, Western Union, and also GITEX Global. Liquid C2 is a business of Cassava Technologies, while Graphiant is a provider of networking infrastructure based in the United States. Research shows that answers in Arabic, Portuguese, and French include news almost as often as those provided in the English language. BuzzStream and Zyte provided data regarding the percentage of news sites that block AI crawlers in different global regions.

Bas Wijne will speak in Cape Town with Sabine Dall’Omo, Strini Mudaly, Shafee Khan, and Victoria Evdokimova at the Africa Tech Festival. He will discuss orchestrating multi-agent systems across the enterprise while hundreds of companies bring their latest news to the event. The articles leave open who will write the content that AI assistants use to answer questions about companies in Africa. It remains unclear how many African publishers will eventually block AI crawlers as they follow the lead of larger global publishers. The partnership between Liquid C2 and Graphiant will migrate enterprises to new algorithms as the global security standards continue evolving.

stories.Headline: Education ministry assigns smart glasses specialists to CSAT sites and rules out postponing exam
stories.Summary:
The articles report that on the 15th police received a voluntary confession from A, the top scorer of the 63rd tax accountant exam, who turned themself in and revealed cheating that used a miniature camera and AI, and police launched an investigation. The confession came the day before reporting by Kyunghyang Shinmun on the 16th, and anxiety grew among students and parents ahead of the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) on the 19th. On the 16th, when the Ministry of Education said it is preparing additional measures, a view of miniature cameras on sale at a camera shop in Seoul was shown, with the ministry noting that for the 2027 CSAT there could be cheating not only using smart glasses but also with miniature cameras. On the 16th, three days before the 2027 academic year CSAT, educational researcher Yeom Dong-ryeol demonstrated cheating with smart glasses during a briefing at the Ministry of Education in the Government Sejong Complex on countermeasures against cheating using smart glasses and micro-cameras. On the 11th, eight days before the 2027 CSAT, during training for dedicated smart-glasses task-force personnel held at the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education in Yongsan-gu, Seoul, a company representative wore smart glasses and demonstrated solving problems.

The Ministry of Education stated on the 16th that technological responses under review, such as signal blocking, face legal and time constraints, and that it is not considering postponing the CSAT. Shin Jin-yong, head of the Admissions Policy Division at the Ministry of Education, said at a briefing held that day at the Government Sejong Complex regarding the possible introduction of AI cheating-detection equipment such as thermal imaging cameras that, given the limited time remaining until the CSAT and the need for uniform test administration, the ministry is reviewing the introduction of such devices with caution. Shin said that under current law, except for matters directly related to national security, signal blocking, so-called Jamming, is not permitted, and that even if allowed, it could interfere with communications around the test sites or impede responses to emergencies. He further noted that a plan to search for smartphones and electronic devices carried by test-takers using metal detectors would require a legal basis and also faces time constraints. Shin said that if all students are treated as potential criminals and body searches are conducted, it becomes difficult to ensure a stable and comfortable testing environment, and he emphasized that the ministry is not considering postponing the CSAT.

The education authorities have prepared measures such as assigning dedicated personnel at each test site to determine whether glasses are smart devices, and the ministry said it will assign at least one specialist for identifying smart glasses to each test site. B, a 12th-grader in Gyeonggi Province, said she usually wears horn-rimmed glasses and is concerned she might be misunderstood for no reason, so she feels she will not be able to focus fully on the test, and smart glasses generally have horn-rimmed designs. C, a parent of a 12th-grader in Seoul's Yangcheon District, said her child has poor eyesight and sometimes wears glasses, and they are considering entering the room without glasses to avoid misunderstanding. Kwon, a 12th-grade student living in Incheon, said the school had advised students to be cautious about wearing horn-rimmed glasses, and that some friends said they did not intend to wear contact lenses instead of glasses because wearing lenses for a long time can worsen dry eye. Yang, who works at an optical shop in Eunpyeong-gu, Seoul, said that ahead of the CSAT there were a few cases in which students with horn-rimmed glasses switched to metal frames because they did not want to be inspected during the exam, and that now, with the CSAT imminent, getting used to new glasses would be hard, so getting a new pair may be difficult.

Kwon said what worries her most is a situation where, even though she did not cheat, she is suspected because of the glasses or belongings she usually carries, causing interference with the test. D, a parent in Gyeonggi Province with a 11th-grade child, said most children will study and prepare diligently, and it would feel unfair if their efforts are not properly evaluated because of the cheating of a few students. C said one person committing a foul can have a butterfly effect that changes the lives and college admissions outcomes of hundreds of thousands, so it must be punished sternly. D said creating a fair testing environment is the responsibility of the education authorities, not of individual students or individual schools. Park, a high school teacher in Gyeonggi Province, said that in most cases, when the glasses are actually checked, the likelihood is high that it is not cheating, but it could lead to complaints if mishandled, and that proctors have no choice but to check cautiously.

Kim, a high school teacher in Seoul, said that when asking students to undergo inspection, he worries about complaints and legal liability, and that although the education authorities have selected inspectors for smart glasses, once the exam begins it is not easy to detect them in the test room. Questions have been raised about whether measures focused solely on smart glasses can block the various forms of AI-enabled cheating. Kwon said there are many ways to use AI, and she worries whether measures that take such possibilities into account can be prepared in the time remaining. Students and parents urged robust measures that prevent cheating while minimizing inconvenience for test-takers. The articles state that detection measures still rely on proctors' visual inspections, raising questions about effectiveness, and that the core of the response by the Ministry of Education to AI-enabled cheating is visual checks by proctors. The articles state that anxiety has grown not only about smart glasses but also about AI-enabled cheating using concealed devices such as micro-cameras.

The articles state that the confession by the top scorer in the tax accountant exam was followed by growing anxiety, and that concerns among CSAT examinees and parents grew after A turned themself in to police the previous day, revealing cheating that used a miniature camera and AI. The articles state that there is worry that intensified monitoring for AI-related cheating and the occurrence of similar misconduct inside test sites could affect the testing environment. The articles state that students worried that the glasses they usually wear might be suspected as smart glasses in the exam room. The articles state that the Ministry of Education said it is preparing additional measures, noting that for the 2027 CSAT there could be cheating not only using smart glasses but also with miniature cameras. The articles state that the ministry said it will assign at least one specialist for identifying smart glasses to each test site.

The articles state that the Ministry of Education is not considering postponing the CSAT, and they leave open whether measures focused solely on smart glasses can block the various forms of AI-enabled cheating. The articles leave open whether measures that take the many ways to use AI into account can be prepared in the time remaining. The articles leave open how proctors will handle inspections given worries about complaints and legal liability, and how detection will work once the exam begins. The articles leave open whether the introduction of AI cheating-detection equipment such as thermal imaging cameras will proceed, which the ministry said it is reviewing with caution. The articles leave open what punishment or outcome will follow the police investigation launched after A's voluntary confession on the 15th.

stories.Headline: US authorities ground flights as Microsoft outage and technical failures spark system stability fears
stories.Summary:
U.S. aviation authorities grounded planes across the country on Friday after a technology upgrade overloaded air traffic control equipment. A Microsoft network issue also disrupted services worldwide on that same day. Officials stated that neither of these incidents showed any signs of malicious activity. The FAA reported that air travel was smoother by Saturday morning. Airline schedules were expected to return to normal by late Sunday.

The FAA ground stop lasted more than four hours and caused intermittent communications and radar gaps. Microsoft said its outage followed a network change and an earlier network capacity upgrade. This outage is believed to have affected many millions of people worldwide. At San Diego International Airport on Saturday, 11 of 62 flights were canceled and 11 were delayed. These events occurred in November 2026 across the United States and globally.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said that airline schedules should be back to normal by late Sunday. Microsoft stated that its services had been fully restored after the network issues. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy made a plea on Friday for tens of billions in more funding. Administration officials explained that the technology upgrade overloaded antiquated equipment. Both the FAA and Microsoft denied that malicious activity caused their respective disruptions.

Chuck Amasio of Rahway, New Jersey, said the events made him think about how wars cripple economies. Maxine Gustafson, a physician assistant from Minneapolis, said the mishaps made her feel afraid and helpless. Tori Perkins from Hawaii expressed doubt about the government's explanations while on a layover in San Diego. Corbyn Wascher, a teacher from Moline, Illinois, praised the American Airlines staff during a four hour tarmac delay. Caroline Ruiz waited at Newark airport for a meal after her trip to Australia was delayed.

Congress approved 12.5 billion dollars for an air traffic control overhaul that began last year. The FAA has replaced thousands of copper wire connections with fiber optic lines and upgraded hundreds of radios. The White House has pushed for an additional 30 billion dollars to complete the air traffic work. Other Friday events included a cruise ship overturning in New Orleans and a bomb found in Illinois. Suspicious drones were also reported over a U.S. air base located in Britain.

Senate Democrats are now demanding clear-cut answers regarding what caused the grounding of the planes. The articles leave open whether the requested 30 billion dollars in additional funding will be approved. It remains unclear if the reliability of technology will improve following these widespread disruptions. The text does not state if the suspicious drones in Britain were ever identified. No further information is provided regarding the investigation into the Illinois bomb.

stories.Headline: CPA Jeong Sook says a perfect Tax Law score is impossible and calls AI cheating a cruel act
stories.Summary:
A contestant from Season 28 of the variety show "I Am Solo," identified as Jung-sook, posted on her social media account on the 15th about the top scorer of the 63rd Tax Attorney Qualification Exam, who had been suspected of using artificial intelligence after an unusually near-perfect score. The person, referred to as Person A, admitted to cheating through electronic devices and AI and turned themselves in, according to the reports. Jung-sook wrote that she is a certified public accountant with 10 years of experience and that she had received many messages from current practitioners and acquaintances asking whether the top score in the tax attorney exam was really possible. She said she replied each time that a perfect score might be possible in Commercial Law or other subjects, but that a perfect score in Tax Law is impossible and the person definitely used AI.

Jung-sook described her own record as a long-term examinee, saying she passed the first stage of the tax attorney exam twice but did not take the second stage, and passed the first stage of the certified public accountant exam three times. She said she failed the second stage of the CPA exam five times and barely passed on her sixth attempt, and that the qualification was hard-won as she rebuilt her foundation starting from middle school math. She said tax law is revised every year and that detailed content such as the National Tax Collection Act cannot be fully memorized no matter how long one studies. She said that even with 10 years of experience she still needs to open a book, and that a perfect score in Tax Law on the time-constrained first-stage exam is impossible.

She said she thinks the incident is a cruel act that tramples on the efforts of other examinees who have persevered quietly, and that it hurts her deeply as a current practitioner. She told colleagues currently in practice that their qualifications are proof of the time they have invested and that she hopes that effort is not devalued by the incident. She also said she hopes the system will be strengthened so that such incidents do not happen again, and she told examinees not to let the news make them overly elated or depressed. She said that even in an era where AI provides answers, it is her accumulated skills that are responsible for clients' numbers in the field, and that even she, who failed five times, eventually made it.

She added that the more we are in the AI era, the more fairly we should compete, and that only qualifications earned that way will protect you for a long time. She said that as a senior who has walked this path, she will cheer for examinees to the end. The reports state that Jung-sook is married to Sang-cheol from the same season and has one son.

stories.Headline: TSMC launches a 500 million dollar fund to invest in chip startups and AI firms
stories.Summary:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company launched a new investment fund of 500 million dollars in November 2026 to support promising chip startups. The world's largest contract chipmaker created this venture fund to back emerging companies that could become future titans like Nvidia or Broadcom. This initiative aims to strengthen the broader semiconductor ecosystem and formalize investment activities during the current boom in artificial intelligence. The company intends to expand its role beyond the manufacturing of advanced processors by investing in various upstream partners. This strategic move allows the firm to identify and support the next generation of leaders in the chip industry.

The 500 million dollar fund targets chip startups, AI model developers, and suppliers of chemicals, advanced materials, and chipmaking equipment. TSMC will also invest up to 500 million dollars each into two major AI model developers named OpenAI and Anthropic. These specific investments, combined with the new arm and existing funds, bring the total investment commitment to 1.7 billion dollars. The new fund is larger than a 200 million dollar emerging fund created in 2021 to help startups develop products. This new strategy includes investing in intellectual property and suppliers, which is a change from the company's previous business practices.

Kevin Zhang is the senior vice president and deputy co-chief operating officer who explained the strategy to Nikkei Asia in Tokyo. He spoke during the Nikkei Forum Global Management Dialogue 2026 and stated that the company wants to support the future's Nvidia. Zhang noted that the returns from the earlier 2021 emerging fund had been exceptional for the company's investment goals. He explained that investing in Anthropic and OpenAI creates a reinforcing loop to build a richer, healthier, and bigger ecosystem. Zhang further mentioned that the company intends to extend its investment scope beyond its immediate customers to broaden its reach.

The fund will affect chip startups and suppliers of materials and equipment who can now receive direct financial backing from TSMC. AI firms like OpenAI and Anthropic are affected because they are exploring custom chips to power their future computing needs. Other industry players are also moving, such as South Korea's SK Hynix, which plans to spend 1.05 billion dollars over five years. SK Hynix aims to support domestic suppliers of semiconductor parts and materials to bolster its supply chain against AI competition. This broader industry trend shows that major chipmakers are increasingly investing in their own supply chains to ensure stability.

TSMC previously operated a 200 million dollar emerging fund in 2021 that helped startups use the company's advanced chip manufacturing technology. The company is now seeing insatiable demand for chips, which has driven the need to broaden its ecosystem for AI. In South Korea, SK Hynix is planning a 600 trillion won project to build four fabrication plants at its Yongin cluster. This cluster will include the Trinity Fab, a testing facility costing 874.6 billion won, funded by the government and SK Hynix. The Trinity Fab is designed to help smaller suppliers test products under conditions similar to commercial chip production lines.

TSMC indicated that it could expand its investment activities further if the company finds it necessary to do so later. The Trinity Fab in Yongin is scheduled to commence its operations in May 2027 to support smaller semiconductor equipment suppliers. SK Hynix will provide up to 50 per cent of initial development costs to suppliers under its research support programme. Financial institutions and SK Hynix will provide 2 trillion won in financing backed by the Korea Trade Insurance Corporation. The articles leave open whether TSMC will increase its total investment commitment beyond the current 1.7 billion dollar figure.

stories.Headline: US government tightens AI chip export rules to limit China's access
stories.Summary:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed a new Commerce Department rule on November 16, 2026, to restrict Chinese access to advanced AI chips. This rule cuts off remote access to chips from Nvidia and other firms located in overseas data centers. The Bureau of Industry and Security issued the interim final rule alongside the National Security Council and Treasury. It targets companies in high risk countries, specifically China, Russia, and Iran, to choke off computing power. The measure takes effect immediately, though it provides a transition period of 90 days for affected companies.

The rule requires export licenses for advanced AI chips and servers sent to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil. It rescinds the Biden era AI Diffusion Rule to close loopholes allowing Chinese firms to rent compute in third countries. Four other bills are circulating, including the AI Overwatch Act and the Chip Security Act to track processor locations. The Remote Access Security Act targets data center rentals, while the Match Act asks allies to limit chipmaking equipment sales. Republicans want these restrictions attached to the annual, must pass defense authorization bill to ensure they actually pass.

Scott Bessent and National Security Adviser Marco Rubio supported the rule to stop Chinese companies from circumventing existing export restrictions. The Bureau of Industry and Security stated the rule was written at the direction of the National Security Council. House Speaker Mike Johnson said on November 12 that a developing consensus exists in Congress regarding limiting chip exports. Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott threatened subpoenas to compel testimony from Howard Lutnick and former CEO Jensen Huang. House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast stated that Jensen Huang had already agreed to testify before the government.

Micron stock fell as much as 7.8 percent, while SK Hynix dropped 5 percent and AMD fell between 4 and 6 percent. Broadcom shares declined around 4 percent as investors worried about hurdles exporting advanced technology to promising international markets. Cloud providers are affected because Nvidia asks them to cap their China business at 49 percent of their services. Lawmakers are scrutinizing Megaspeed, a Singapore company suspected of smuggling restricted Nvidia chips into China, and criticizing Howard Lutnick. A federal court also allowed an antitrust lawsuit alleging DRAM price fixing against Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix.

Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO and board member after 33 years amid reports of a relationship with a suspected spy. CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO after Huang spent much of 2025 arguing that sales limits would backfire. In April 2025, Nvidia took a 5.5 billion dollar charge when licenses were required for its H20 chip. AMD warned of a hit up to 800 million dollars during that same period of increased regulatory pressure. Taiwanese prosecutors raided Nvidia offices on July 28 and detained an employee during a widening AI chip smuggling probe.

Nvidia has not yet named a permanent CEO, and no vote on the defense bill chip language has been scheduled. Reuters expects Jensen Huang to testify before November 26, though other timelines for his appearance may vary. Democrats signal they will take broader action after they take the House majority in January 2027. Neither AMD nor Nvidia has stated what the costs of the four new proposed bills would be. The articles leave open whether the antitrust price fixing allegations against Micron and its peers will lead to liability.

stories.Headline: Hong Kong police deploy AI facial recognition across city surveillance network
stories.Summary:
Hong Kong rolled out AI facial recognition across its CCTV network on November 16, 2026, to expand monitoring of public spaces. The police implemented these new functions to help with national security, crime prevention, and the tracking of various criminal suspects. This rollout happened on a Monday and follows a period of tightened control by China over the city's finance hub. The government intends to use these artificial intelligence tools to increase the overall capabilities of existing surveillance systems in the city. This expansion of monitoring is being carried out under a specific police operation that has been dubbed as SmartView.

The SmartView operation launched in 2024 and has already seen roughly 5,000 closed-circuit television cameras installed across the city of Hong Kong. These existing cameras are credited with solving nearly 2,200 cases and leading to more than 2,800 arrests since the launch. Security chief Chris Tang told lawmakers in 2025 that the AI will monitor crowds, read licence plates, and track suspects. Documents submitted to the legislature state that authorities plan to increase the total number of cameras to 60,000 by 2028. These tools are designed to be a safeguard for law-abiding citizens while enhancing the police ability to monitor public areas.

Police commissioner Joe Chow announced the rollout over the weekend and stated the system would be a safeguard for law-abiding citizens. He told local media on November 15 that he understands people may be concerned, but the new system won't be abused. Security chief Chris Tang previously explained to lawmakers that the AI functions would naturally be applied to people to track suspects. These officials maintain that the expansion of the camera network is necessary for the purposes of crime prevention and national security. The police believe that the AI tools will significantly boost the effectiveness of their current surveillance and law enforcement operations.

A finance worker in his 40s named Li told AFP he worried about misuse because data and facial images are collected. Another resident named Saturday Zhou said people are used to such cameras in mainland cities but officials must maintain data transparency. International rights groups and non-governmental organisations have expressed concern over the massive scale of AI surveillance already used in mainland China. Critics argue that this technology grants the government unchecked power to invade privacy and could lead to wrongful arrests via matches. Many residents and rights groups warn about the dangers of constant monitoring, weak transparency, and the possibility of false facial matches.

China tightened control over Hong Kong after huge pro-democracy protests swept the city in 2019 by imposing a national security law. Critics say this law has quelled dissent, while mainland China already uses AI surveillance on a massive scale for its government. A 2025 report by the Australian Strategic Policy Institute warned that AI tools enable China to automate censorship and suppress dissent. Similar surveillance technology has been adopted in Britain, though the European Union banned real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces in 2024. The EU ban on these law enforcement systems includes some exceptions, but generally restricts the use of such biometric identification tools.

The police will continue to install more cameras until they reach the goal of 60,000 units by the year 2028. Authorities will use the AI to monitor crowds and read licence plates as part of the ongoing SmartView police operation. The articles leave open whether the government will increase transparency regarding how the collected facial and personal data is used. It remains unclear if the concerns regarding false matches and wrongful arrests will be addressed by the Hong Kong police department. There is no information on whether Hong Kong will adopt any restrictions similar to the biometric identification ban seen in Europe.

stories.Headline: Nvidia and other AI stocks drag US markets lower amid leadership changes and regulatory fears
stories.Summary:
Manic swings for Nvidia and other artificial intelligence stocks dragged the United States market lower on Tuesday, November 17, 2026. The S&P 500 sank 1.1 percent and nearly faced its first back to back losses of 1.5 percent since March. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 779 points, or 1.5 percent, as of 11:30 a.m. Eastern time that day. The Nasdaq composite dropped 1.2 percent while Nvidia veered lower and dropped as much as 3.7 percent before paring losses. Other AI stocks like Advanced Micro Devices and CoreWeave also flipped from early morning gains to losses of 2.1 and 1.3 percent.

Nvidia is creating a new board committee to oversee global trade compliance and national security in New York and other places. This change follows revelations that former CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with an alleged spy for China during his tenure. Interim CEO Colette Kress is scheduled to deliver the latest earnings report after trading ends for the day on Tuesday. The 10 year Treasury yield climbed toward 5.15 percent Tuesday morning from 5.12 percent late Monday before pulling back to 5.10 percent. Brent crude oil rose 1 percent to 93.36 dollars per barrel amid uncertainty about the war with Iran.

Interim CEO Colette Kress is responsible for speaking to Wall Street for the first time since taking over for Jensen Huang. Jensen Huang stated on the X social network that he would return if the Board decides it is in the best interest. He mentioned that his return should benefit shareholders, employees, the company, and America if the Board of Directors chooses that path. The pressure is now on Kress and Nvidia to show if the company can continue its tremendous growth after the resignation. These leaders must address whether the company can maintain its influence following the departure of one of the strongest AI influencers.

Investors in AI stocks are affected by worries that prices shot too high and that high interest rates limit borrowed growth money. Others fear that Democratic victories in the November midterm elections could lead to tougher regulations and restrictions on AI data centers. Home Depot sank 2.3 percent because expensive mortgage rates chilled the housing market, while JPMorgan Chase fell 2.1 percent on spending concerns. United Airlines lost 3.3 percent after a system outage lasted over 90 minutes and oil prices rose for the carrier. The Walt Disney Co. rose 0.7 percent after reporting stronger revenue for the latest quarter than analysts had originally expected.

AI stocks have been shaky for months because they are some of the most valuable and influential on Wall Street today. High oil prices, high inflation, and other factors have caused Treasury yields to climb, which in turn increased expensive mortgage rates. A report showed that an underlying measure of spending at U.S. retailers was stronger last month than economists had expected. Big businesses across the S&P 500 are on track for summer earnings per share nearly 32 percent higher than last year. In abroad markets, South Korea's Kospi fell 2.6 percent to its lowest closing level since February according to the provided articles.

Nvidia will deliver its latest earnings report after trading ends for the day to show if its tremendous growth can continue. Investors will watch to see if the new board committee can successfully oversee national security and global trade compliance moving forward. The market remains uncertain about how much pain the broad U.S. economy will feel from any pullback in AI related spending. It is unclear if the Board of Directors will decide that the return of Jensen Huang is in the best interest. The articles leave open whether the U.S. market will recover from these manic swings or continue to drag lower over time.

stories.Headline: SnapLogic launches MCP Discovery Hub and partners with Honeycomb for AI agent observability
stories.Summary:
SnapLogic announced new advancements to its Agentic Integration and Applied AI Platform on Nov. 17, 2026 at INTEGRATEAI 2026 in London, including the launch of Discovery Hub, a centralized registry for discovering and reusing Model Context Protocol servers and tools. The company also introduced expanded agent-building capabilities in SnapCode, enhanced pipeline governance and persistent conversations in SnapGPT, and plans for new Agent Observability capabilities. SnapLogic announced a partnership with Honeycomb, the observability platform built for the AI era, to help enterprises see what their AI agents and connected systems are doing in one trace. Tipalti announced AP Agent, a next-generation agentic AI product designed to manage the complete accounts payable lifecycle, from invoice capture and coding through to approvals, payments and reconciliation. Tipalti also introduced Model Context Protocol capabilities that connect its financial data to enterprise AI tools such as Claude Enterprise.

Discovery Hub provides a searchable, environment-wide catalog of published MCP servers and their tools, and developers can copy working client configurations for Claude Code, Cursor, or VS Code. Discovery Hub combines with SnapLogic's governance and observability capabilities to form the MCP gateway for an organization's environment, with API management policies controlling access and Monitor providing visibility into MCP server usage. New SnapCode skills enable developers to build agent pipelines consisting of a driver pipeline and supporting tool pipelines, as well as MCP server pipelines that expose pipelines as tools, with browser-based sign-in with single sign-on and multifactor authentication support, session health checks, and update management. SnapGPT now enables developers to analyze pipelines against organizational standards configured in Admin Manager, filter findings, and apply recommended fixes, and new persistent sessions allow users to save and return to previous conversations with their full context intact. New tools added to SnapLogic MCP Server support project renaming, task discovery and pipeline standards validation, along with asynchronous pipeline execution and validation and credential-safe task details.

Jeremiah Stone, CTO of SnapLogic, said the more MCP servers an enterprise deploys, the harder it becomes to keep track of what has already been built, what is being used, and whether teams are following the same standards. Stone said that without a shared approach to discovery and governance, organizations create more complexity and fragility instead of making progress, and that the next phase of agentic AI depends on making these capabilities easier to find, reuse, and manage at scale. Stone said enterprises are moving from asking whether AI agents will work to asking whether they can trust them to perform, and that trust and performance both start with visibility. Stone said Honeycomb gives SnapLogic customers a trace of everything an agent does through the systems SnapLogic connects, so they can govern AI with confidence and improve it continuously. Roby Baruch, chief product and technology officer at Tipalti, said the company's aim is to give finance leaders the confidence to reimagine what their teams and their businesses can achieve as AI agents take on more autonomous responsibilities.

Matt Nelson, President, Go-To-Market at Honeycomb, said Honeycomb customers are building software that no longer behaves in a predictable way and need to see what is really happening with their systems in production. Nelson said SnapLogic provides the operational layer that securely connects and orchestrates AI agents, applications and data across the enterprise, while Honeycomb brings the visibility needed to understand how those interactions unfold. Nelson said the two companies can follow a request from the first prompt, through the AI agent, into the business systems behind it, and back again, and that shared view lets engineering and operations teams investigate problems quickly and build AI they can rely on. Tipalti, based in Foster City, processes more than $100 billion in annualised payment volume across 120 currencies for around 6,500 customers. Tipalti's AP Agent is built around a configurable human-in-the-loop model, and finance teams can define which activities the agent executes autonomously and which require a human sign-off, with field-level reasoning surfaced to explain AI-generated values.

Every Tipalti action is logged in a full audit trail, and users can interrogate, clarify or override individual decisions through natural-language conversation, and the company says the agent applies corrections from user feedback to future processing, improving accuracy over time. Tipalti did not publish independent benchmark data for processing accuracy or straight-through reconciliation rates in the announcement. Agent Observability will provide detailed visibility into SnapLogic agents built in Agent Creator, building on existing observability features in Monitor, and teams will be able to trace individual agent runs, including the tools called, their sequence, execution times, and results. Self-healing functionality in SnapGPT and SnapCode, building on SnapLogic's existing Introspection capabilities, will enable AI-assisted recommendations and fixes for common pipeline problems, including incorrect expressions, missing properties, and transient execution failures, with configurable approval controls, automated validation, rollback safeguards, and audit logging. The SnapLogic platform is built on connections to more than 1,000 applications and data sources, and Honeycomb is built on a decade of distributed tracing leadership and deep roots in the OpenTelemetry community.

Tipalti's announcement extends work the company began in 2025 when it introduced a first generation of specialised AI agents. AP Agent is designed to orchestrate entire workflows, drawing on vendor history, general ledger data and company-specific accounting policies to make context-aware decisions rather than following static rule sets. SnapLogic's platform serves as the AI operational layer for the enterprise, securely connecting applications, data, APIs and AI agents across cloud, on-premise and hybrid environments, and is trusted by global enterprises including AstraZeneca, Adobe, Verizon, and Sony. Honeycomb gives engineering teams and the AI agents now operating alongside them real-time, high-cardinality answers about any production system, with no pre-aggregation and no cardinality limits. The partnership is part of a wider shift in how enterprise system landscapes are evolving as AI agents move from pilots into transforming business operations, and agents do not stay inside one application, as a single request can pass through a customer system, a data warehouse, a finance platform, and an AI model within seconds.

Discovery Hub for SnapLogic-native MCP servers, SnapCode agent building capabilities, SnapGPT enhanced pipeline governance and SnapGPT persistent sessions are generally available now. Discovery Hub with third-party MCP server support, self-healing integrations and Agent Observability capabilities will be generally available in the coming months. SnapLogic's Agentic Integration and Applied AI Platform is the governed layer that gives agents secure access to systems with the right permissions, context, and controls in place, and the partnership with Honeycomb adds a complete picture of what happens next. Customers have told both companies that it is no longer enough to monitor the edges of the factory, that they want to know what is happening inside their core systems, and that they want to follow a single piece of work from start to finish with the context that explains it. Honeycomb's approach, which follows each request through every service it touches, now extends across the connections SnapLogic manages, which matters more for AI because agents are non-deterministic and do not behave the same way twice, and what they do depends on the context they are given.

stories.Headline: LG Energy Solution showcases integrated AI data center power infrastructure at RE+ 2026
stories.Summary:
LG Energy Solution showcased integrated power infrastructure for AI data centers at RE+ 2026, which took place November 17 to 19 at the Las Vegas Convention Center. The company exhibited under the theme "Powering Future of AI - Reliable. Resilient. Intelligent." Its booth was organized into five zones: Hero, Grid-Scale Storage System, Next-Gen Battery Technologies, Critical Power Solutions for AI Data Centers, and LG Energy Solution Vertech. The company presented the JF2 AC LINK, a BESS solution that qualified as NVIDIA DSX Ready BESS. Visitors could find LG Energy Solution at Booth C4708 in the Central Hall.

The Hero Zone showed BESS, a UPS battery solution, battery backup units and energy management systems working together as integrated AIDC power infrastructure. The Grid-Scale Storage System Zone showed JF3 LINK, a grid-scale ESS built with U.S.-manufactured LFP batteries and engineered for AIDCs and power grids. Its optimized layout improves site-level energy density by approximately 26% compared with conventional systems. It features a multi-layer safety architecture with thermal barriers designed to prevent thermal propagation, and it uses digital twin technology and AI-powered software. The Next-Gen Battery Technologies Zone presented a concept combining sodium-ion batteries (SIB LINK) with solid-state transformer (SST) technology.

SIB LINK offers supply chain resilience, stable performance in low-temperature environments and high thermal stability, while SSTs enable rapid response to sudden changes in power demand and help reduce power conversion losses. The Critical Power Solutions for AI Data Centers Zone showed the next-generation JP6 UPS battery solution and a BBU solution based on 2170 cylindrical cells. The JP6 delivers market-leading power density, while the BBU provides immediate backup power to servers during power outages and features a space-efficient battery design. The LG Energy Solution Vertech Zone highlighted the U.S. energy storage division's End-to-End One-Stop Solution across the entire ESS lifecycle. It also presented AEROS Suite, an integrated software platform for ESS operations, optimization, analytics and revenue generation.

Chang Beom Kang, Head of the ESS Battery Division at LG Energy Solution, said the exhibition would demonstrate the company's capabilities as an integrated energy platform company that goes beyond battery manufacturing. He said the company would continue to accelerate its growth in North America by leveraging differentiated technologies, including next-generation battery systems, and its strong localization strategy. Kang Chang-beom said stable power storage and supply and efficient operations are essential for the growth of the AI industry. He said the company would grow into an energy platform company by combining its North American production base, battery technology, and system construction and intelligent operations capabilities. AEROS Intelligence, the newest addition to the software suite, transforms energy storage system data into actionable insights.

AEROS Intelligence can help customers defer battery augmentation for around 1.5 years and preserve millions in capital value over the life of the project, according to the company. By the end of 2026, LG Energy Solution plans to secure more than 50 GWh of ESS production capacity in North America. Samsung SDI and LG Energy Solution both attended RE+ 2026, which draws about 1,300 companies and some 40,000 visitors. LG Energy Solution set up the largest exhibition booth among South Korean battery makers at 279 square meters, about 20% larger than last year. Samsung SDI exhibited under the theme "AI Thinks, Battery Enables," showcasing its all-in-one ESS SBB 2.0, based on LFP prismatic batteries produced locally in the United States.

Samsung SDI's SBB 2.0 packs battery cells and safety devices into a 20-foot container, and the company recently completed its local production system and is preparing for full-scale supply. For AI data center UPS applications, Samsung SDI highlighted the U8A3, a prismatic battery using lithium manganese oxide material, which it says became the world's first to pass all criteria in the large-scale indoor fire test administered by UL Solutions. In the BBU segment, Samsung SDI planned to unveil high-output, high-capacity cylindrical batteries and product lines based on nickel-cobalt-manganese and LFP chemistries. In South Korea, the third ESS central contracting auction, which LG Energy Solution is sitting out, has become a two-way race between Samsung SDI and SK On at 1,180MW. The auction totals 1,180MW, or about 7.08GWh in storage capacity, the largest ever, and is larger than the first and second rounds combined.

Samsung SDI's South Korean production capacity is about 15GWh, with roughly 5GWh of remaining supply capacity, while SK On's LFP capacity for ESS is about 3GWh, converted from an EV line in Seosan with deliveries due in the first half of next year. The combined spare volume of the two is about 8GWh. With the number of suppliers reduced from three to two, observers expect the low-price bidding competition seen in the first and second rounds to ease. A battery industry official said the three companies had shifted to a profit-making trend in the second half of this year and are expected to focus on profitability-oriented fundamentals rather than enduring cutthroat competition as in the past. The official said additional demand is also waiting in the fourth and fifth auctions, so the incentive to cut prices excessively has diminished.

LG Energy Solution's absence from the auction is seen as a strategic judgment prioritizing profitability and fulfillment of existing orders over volume expansion. The company said it will focus on stably carrying out volumes it has already secured, including the South Korean government's "AI-enabled distribution grid ESS construction support project," for which it was selected in July. Some note that with the operator holding the largest South Korean production capacity sitting out, supply capacity could become tight relative to the order volume, but for the two remaining suppliers this strengthens their pricing power. Samsung SDI's prismatic NCA batteries, which emphasize fire safety, are expected to face off against SK On's pouch-type LFP batteries, which play up LFP's status as the mainstream chemistry in the global ESS market. The two companies' emphasis on US-made batteries and local assembly and production systems is also a move mindful of tariffs and supply chain regulations.

Throughout the event, LG Energy Solution hosted expert sessions at its booth on topics including "LG Energy Solution's Preparedness for AI Data Centers," "Energy Storage for AI Data Centers: Understanding Integration" and "AEROS Intelligence." Through these sessions, the company highlights its differentiated capabilities in AI data center power solutions, from infrastructure deployment and system integration to operations. LG Energy Solution is a leading global manufacturer of lithium-ion batteries for electric vehicles, mobility, IT and energy storage systems, with more than 30 years of experience in battery technology and extensive research and development. The company is the top battery-related patent holder in the world with over 100,000 patents, and its global network spans North America, Europe and Asia, including battery manufacturing facilities established through joint ventures with major automakers. LG Energy Solution aims to achieve carbon neutrality across its value chain by 2050.

Samsung SDI is making rapid response through local production its differentiator, while LG Energy Solution is betting on platform capabilities spanning production to operations. Market attention now shifts to North America, where AI data centers draw enormous amounts of power around the clock while carrying both instantaneous load fluctuations and blackout risks, fueling rapid growth in demand for integrated power solutions spanning grid-scale ESS, UPS and BBU. As AI data center investment surges, storage systems that can respond to fluctuations in power demand and uninterruptible power supplies are growing more important, and both companies are targeting North American orders by emphasizing their US production capacity. The two companies disclosed their participation plans on Nov. 15. The articles leave open what orders the two companies will secure in North America and how the fourth and fifth South Korean auctions will unfold.
