stories.Headline: Stanford researchers open source Memorilla to provide latent semantic memory for frozen LLMs
stories.Summary:
Researchers at Stanford University developed Memorilla, a latent semantic memory system for large language models, which was released in November 2026. This open source system condenses entire document collections into a fixed number of query dependent memory tokens for frozen models. It allows these frozen models to process extensive data with improved accuracy and efficiency while significantly reducing total token usage. The system reads a whole document collection and provides the model with just 16 memory tokens for each question. This approach achieves better average performance than other methods such as Mem0 and MemoRAG, according to the research team.

The system requires Linux with CUDA GPUs and Python 3.11, using NVIDIA H100 80GB GPUs for its training recipes. It utilizes a 194M parameter trainable memory module with a frozen Qwen3-Embedding-4B encoder and a frozen Qwen3-8B decoder. Training takes 19 hours on four H100 GPUs, downloading 310 GiB of data and embeddings across three distinct stages. The first stage uses 1.98M Wikipedia examples, the second adds 1.34M QA examples, and the third fine tunes on benchmarks. Checkpoints are available on Hugging Face at memorilla/Memorilla-Qwen3-8B under the Apache 2.0 license for public use and deployment.

The work comes from Jure Leskovec's SNAP group, with co authors from MIT, Penn, and the University of Toronto. The researchers stated that Memorilla learns what each question needs from the whole store rather than using retrieval chunks. They reported that the system achieves 84.33 per cent accuracy on FactKG, which is higher than the 80.43 per cent full context. The team noted that the memory module can scale to millions of tokens while consistently using only 16 memory tokens. They also claimed the highest reported average across eight benchmarks, with a score of 49.68 for the system.

The system affects frozen LLMs by removing the need for full context prompting, which slows down as history grows. It outperforms xRAG on PersonaMem-v2 with 44.60 per cent accuracy, compared to 30.90 per cent for the next best method. However, it performs worse on PubMedQA, scoring 59.00 per cent against 69.00 per cent for LLMLingua-2 due to small abstract sizes. MemoRAG leads on NarrativeQA ROUGE-L with 20.51 versus 19.31 and on PersonalizationV4 with 67.88 per cent versus 66.65 per cent. The system also helps agents, raising the average success rate on TextWorld games from 18.6 per cent to 24.2 per cent.

Full context prompting is slower than Memorilla, which answers in 0.74 seconds for 512 documents versus 19.9 seconds for full context. The system can compress books and movie scripts from NarrativeQA by over 4,000 times, replacing 67,385 tokens with 16 tokens. A memory cache can reduce processing for one million documents to 8.1 milliseconds, or 5.0 milliseconds using torch.compile. This cache costs 80 GiB at four million documents, where a question takes 33 milliseconds to process on one B200. The research team also released PersonalizationV4, featuring 149 synthetic users with 200 conversations each under a CC BY 4.0 license.

Users can install the system with uv on Linux and load the model using the MemoryVLLM.from_pretrained function for deployment. The first run requires downloading about 25 GB of models, and custom data needs parquet files with specific column names. Each checkpoint must run with the specific decoder it was trained with to ensure the evaluation documents remain accurate. The articles leave open whether any quantized variants of the memory module will be disclosed for users with smaller GPUs. They do not state if the system will be expanded to support decoders other than the Qwen3 series.

stories.Headline: A man surnamed Han admits using AI smart glasses to cheat on national accountant exams
stories.Summary:
A thirty four year old man surnamed Han admitted on Sunday that he cheated on national exams using generative artificial intelligence. He confessed on a YouTube channel that he used electronic devices to cheat during the first round of the tax accountant exam. Han also admitted to cheating on the second round of that exam and the first round of the certified public accountant exam. He turned himself in to the police after facing allegations that he used AI equipped smart glasses to commit fraud. This scandal has sent shockwaves throughout the nation and exposed a lack of safeguards against AI assisted misconduct in South Korea.

Han scored 397.5 out of 400 in the April first round exam, with perfect scores in three subjects and one missed finance question. Three months later, he scored 663 out of 800 in the second stage written examination and was named the overall top scorer. The Ministry of Finance and Economy moved to suspend his certification, while the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency Public Crime Investigation Unit investigates. Policy Chief Ha Joon Kyung chaired a meeting on November 15, four days before the 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test. Two proctors were assigned to the classroom where Han took the test, but they did not detect his fraudulent behavior.

Prime Minister Han Seong sook called for comprehensive measures to protect the fairness and credibility of state examinations during a Monday meeting. She stated that those who worked hard to prepare for exams should not be disadvantaged by the cheating of other candidates. The Prime Minister added that such misconduct should not undermine public trust in competitive examinations and required measures before and after tests. Presidential chief of staff Lim Kwang hyun told reporters on Sunday that the government was working to find solutions for the crisis. A presidential official stated that the office is taking the matter very seriously because the college entrance exam takes place next week.

Kim Yong jae, the 2018 top scorer, said that earning a perfect score in even one subject is virtually impossible for candidates. He noted that candidates have only 80 minutes to answer 80 accounting questions, suggesting the top scorer was either a genius or cheater. The Financial Services Commission came under fire for failing to detect the cheating, while the public expressed growing concerns over exam integrity. Other national certification examinations were held before the tax accountant exam, raising questions about whether cheating occurred in those other tests. The scandal affects the credibility of state administered exams and the trust of students who prepare honestly for these competitive tests.

The articles state that the nation has focused too much on competing for AI leadership and too little on necessary institutional safeguards. There was a widespread belief that AI is inherently beneficial, creating a gap between technological ambition and the actual institutional preparedness. The editorial argues that after the fact responses are insufficient and that the nation is unprepared for the age of artificial intelligence. Proctors lacked the tools and technology needed to identify AI assisted cheating, making it impossible for them to notice the misconduct. The government has belatedly scrambled to introduce measures in response to the scandal as the college entrance exam approached on Thursday.

Officials are now discussing preemptive detection measures and advanced technologies capable of thwarting AI assisted misconduct before the nationwide college entrance exam. The Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education held a training session on November 11 regarding a smart glasses cheating prevention guide in Yongsan gu. The government is working to find solutions to ensure that no more AI assisted cheating occurs during the upcoming scholastic ability test. It remains questionable whether the nation is prepared to build the necessary infrastructure to detect such high tech fraud in the future. The articles leave open whether other national certification exams were compromised by similar AI tools before the confession of the man.

stories.Headline: Jensen Huang resigns as NVIDIA CEO amid personal scandals and reports of restricted chip sales in China
stories.Summary:
Reuters published an investigation on November 13, 2026, regarding NVIDIA's business in China. The report found that Chinese demand for restricted hardware continued despite official company guidance. This news arrived during the same week that CBS News reported Jensen Huang's resignation. Huang stepped down as chief executive following reports of personal scandals and affairs. One affair involved a former executive at Megaspeed who allegedly has ties to Chinese intelligence.

NVIDIA guided to zero China revenue for four straight quarters, including Q3 guidance of 108 billion dollars. In Q1 FY2027, the company shipped no H20 compute products to China, compared with 4.6 billion dollars previously. Reuters found over 150 Chinese contracts worth 23 billion yuan, or 3.2 billion dollars, using H100, H200, and H800 chips. IDC estimates NVIDIA held 34% of Chinese AI-accelerator shipments in the first half of 2026. These projects include some that are running, some under construction, and some still planned.

CFO Collette Kress stated on August 26 that no China data center compute revenue was in the forward outlook. She described licensed Hopper 200 shipments to China as dilutive to corporate gross margins and under 1% of revenue. Jensen Huang said that unconstrained demand would be a lot higher than the 70% they could deliver. He explained that compute is revenue and that losing China barely dented the company's overall results. Kress has now stepped in as the interim CEO and longtime board member.

Analysts and reporters noted that the entire AI economy is built on top of NVIDIA. Rebecca Bellan stated that Huang is NVIDIA and expressed surprise at his resignation. Some believe the leadership change and U.S. scrutiny now imperil the restricted chip projects in China. This situation raises export-control risks for a company that told investors to expect zero China revenue. The stock closed at 162.85 dollars on November 13, down 26.41% for the month.

In 2025, Huang said NVIDIA's China market share fell from 95% to zero after U.S. export restrictions. The company reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of 96.22 billion dollars, which was up 105.8% year over year. Non-GAAP EPS reached 2.22 dollars, beating the estimate of 2.09 dollars, with data center revenue at 89.02 billion dollars. Intelligence circles reportedly knew about Huang's relationship with Alice Huang nearly a year before the public did. Trump was given warnings about the affair but reportedly did not mind.

The NVIDIA board is currently investigating Huang's relationship with the alleged Chinese intelligence asset. Lawmakers are pushing for chip limits in the defense bill following the spy scandal. The company must now manage expenses under the caretaker appointment of the interim CEO. It remains open whether the board's probe will reveal if national security was threatened. The articles leave open if any licensed reopening of the China market will add to forecasts.

stories.Headline: Ramaphosa leads South African delegation in Silicon Valley to study AI development and adoption
stories.Summary:
President Cyril Ramaphosa arrived in California in the United States of America on Saturday, 14 November 2026, for a working visit to Silicon Valley, where he is leading a high-level, multi-stakeholder South African delegation to gain insights into the global artificial intelligence ecosystem and to inform South Africa's approach to the development, adoption and application of AI. The delegation comprises representatives from government, academia, business, research institutions, technical experts and university students, which the Presidency says reflects the country's commitment to an inclusive, collaborative and multi-stakeholder approach to harnessing the opportunities presented by AI. The programme includes engagements with leading technology companies, investors, researchers, academics and AI experts, as well as technology demonstrations and knowledge exchanges, which provide an opportunity to explore developments in frontier AI, robotics, data infrastructure, cloud computing, digital innovation and the practical application of AI across various sectors. A key component of the visit is engagements with leading academic institutions, focusing on the implications of AI for technology, security, the economy, business and the labour market, as well as emerging developments in robotics and technological research.

The programme also features the South Africa AI Opportunity gathering, under the theme Building the African AI Economy: Infrastructure, Investment and Innovation, which brings together South African and international stakeholders to explore how South Africa can position itself as a competitive AI hub on the African continent. Discussions there focus on AI infrastructure, data centres, computing capacity, energy requirements, investment opportunities and the growth of a competitive start-up ecosystem, while other areas of engagement include the application of AI in government and industry, law enforcement and public safety, AI safety and security, governance, skills development and the future of work. The delegation also engages with technology and infrastructure companies to gain insights into emerging technologies, investment trends and developments shaping the global AI ecosystem, and these interactions seek to identify opportunities for investment, knowledge exchange, skills development and the strengthening of South Africa's technological capabilities. The Presidency says AI presents significant opportunities to improve productivity, strengthen public service delivery, stimulate economic growth and support the creation of new industries and employment opportunities, with potential applications in South Africa including health, education, criminal justice, public administration and public procurement.

The visit provides an opportunity to learn from countries and institutions at the forefront of AI development, understand the associated risks and challenges, and consider how South Africa can develop an enabling policy, regulatory and skills environment to support responsible AI adoption. It also promotes South Africa as an investment destination, showcases progress in economic reforms, including through Operation Vulindlela, and highlights opportunities for investment in the country's digital economy, research capacity and innovation ecosystem. South Africa seeks to harness the transformative potential of AI while safeguarding digital sovereignty, policy autonomy, data protection and responsible AI governance, ensuring that technological advancement contributes meaningfully to inclusive economic growth and development. The President is accompanied by the Ministers of Finance; International Relations and Cooperation; Science, Technology and Innovation; Trade, Industry and Competition; Communications and Digital Technologies; Electricity and Energy; Small Business Development; and the Presidency, as well as South Africa's Ambassador to the United States of America, and media enquiries are directed to Vincent Magwenya, Spokesperson to the President.

stories.Headline: Armin Ashenberg argues universities must teach graduates to collaborate with AI as automation reshapes the job market
stories.Summary:
Dr Armin D Ashenberg of the School of Law at Western Sydney University wrote an opinion piece first published with full links on The Conversation. The piece was also published by Western Sydney University on 16 November 2026. It addresses concerns about artificial intelligence taking people's jobs and reducing job opportunities for university graduates. AI software companies such as OpenAI, Google DeepMind and Anthropic are pursuing AI systems capable of matching or exceeding human performance across a broad range of intellectual tasks. The article asks what this means for graduates and universities and which jobs are most at risk.

A federal government report published in July rated jobs typically involving cognitive tasks as those with the highest exposure to AI automation, including accountants, clerks and receptionists. Jobs rated as lowest exposure tended to require more physical work, such as tradies, carers and truck drivers. The report found that as of February this year AI had not had significant impacts on the Australian job market, including graduate opportunities. This month the Reserve Bank of Australia noted some signs younger workers in more AI-exposed industries are struggling to find work in Australia. The number of graduate jobs in some law firms has been slashed, with low-level tasks passed onto AI, and consulting firms have also cut graduate roles in recent years but claim it is not because of AI.

Just last week Qantas announced it will outsource 850 jobs to India while investing more in AI. A 2024 study compared the reasoning skills of humans and AI language models through tests including maths puzzles designed to assess whether people and AI models could recognise that an answer, which seems right at first, is actually wrong. In the example given, a scarf costs 210€ more than a hat, the scarf and the hat cost 220€ in total, and the correct answer for the hat is 5€. Researchers found earlier AI systems performed worse than human participants in the study's reasoning test, while more recent AI models performed better. An OpenAI model recently disproved a longstanding conjecture in geometry dating back to 1946.

Ashenberg's own research analysed AI's responses on university criminal law exams in 2023 and 2025, finding average exam scores improved from 52.5% in 2023 to 76.3% in 2025. Unlike the 2023 study, the 2025 models on average performed better than an average university student on critical thinking capabilities. These were specific tests and do not prove AI could displace humans and take over an entire profession, but the results challenge the assumption AI weaknesses will remain unchanged. Robotaxis carry passengers in a growing number of cities, delivery robots bring meals to customers and autonomous excavators dig on construction sites. In a 2026 pilot study health-care professionals, mostly nurses, accepted half the deliberately wrong AI recommendations and passed over about one in six correct ones.

In a study looking at how the UK public uses AI for medical advice, researchers found people sometimes left out important details when consulting chatbots, so the chatbots sometimes mixed useful suggestions with misleading ones. The article is part of a series on how AI is reshaping higher education, taking a deeper look into how AI has disrupted degrees, how universities are responding and what the technology means for the sector's future. The article states that if a sufficiently capable AI could control reliable, affordable robots then electricians and plumbers could also face competition. It adds that despite significant progress in robots' ability to carry out complex physical tasks it is still unclear how soon they will be able to do more of the work tradies do. For now, students who choose vocational pathways such as apprenticeships may face a lower risk of AI-related job disruption.

The article argues the possibility of humans working with AI should be central to how universities prepare students for the workforce, because if a worker can't improve the quality or efficiency of AI's output an employer may have little economic reason to involve them. It says graduates may need to understand what a good result looks like when using AI, recognise when AI falls short, and have the knowledge and skills to improve AI's output. It says they also need to learn how to collaborate with AI, how to direct it, question its output and persist until the result is better than what it produced initially. It states universities can't simply replace disciplinary knowledge with AI skills, and students will need the knowledge and skills their degrees have always required as well as the ability to collaborate effectively with AI. It concludes that a technology designed to make our lives easier may actually require us to work harder to stay relevant in the job market.

stories.Headline: Gartner analyst warns India risks losing economic value by exporting AI training data
stories.Summary:
Arun Chandrasekaran, a Distinguished VP Analyst at Gartner, warned on November 17, 2026, that India might become a mere exporter of data for artificial intelligence. He noted that global companies and startups are currently using the country as a collection ground for embodied robotics and physical AI. This trend allows foreign entities to train models on how to navigate the physical world using Indian data. Consequently, the nation risks losing the economic value generated from these massive data contributions.

Strengthening national capabilities requires improving data quality, privacy standards, and the availability of government datasets for innovation. Chandrasekaran identified research, data, and computing infrastructure as the three foundational requirements for any country building AI. He suggested focusing on specialized applications and speech-aware models for the multilingual population rather than competing with China or the US. This shift is necessary because India currently lacks the strong data-sharing and privacy frameworks needed to monetize its information.

The analyst expressed that it is unfortunate India cannot currently monetize the value of its exported data. He mentioned that while OpenAI sees India as its largest market by weekly users, this adoption does not automatically benefit local businesses. Chandrasekaran also shared that over 50 per cent of Gartner clients feel they are not receiving sufficient value from AI agents. He clarified that the market is undergoing a recalibration rather than a retreat from the technology.

Investors are now shifting their interest toward vertical AI, cybersecurity, and the data context layer instead of expensive foundational models. Enterprises are moving away from experimental projects to focus on use cases where benefits can be measured. This change comes as buyers discontinue projects that fail to demonstrate clear returns on investment. India must now leverage its established sectors to create AI applications that serve its specific domestic needs.

stories.Headline: Uber exits Nigeria and launches London robotaxis with Wayve as drivers describe falling pay
stories.Summary:
On 2 September, Uber confirmed it was discontinuing its operations in Nigeria after 12 years in one of Africa's biggest markets, and it announced a similar exercise in Uganda. Uber said the decision followed a review of its business priorities and investment focus across Africa. The next day, 3 September, Uber and British AI company Wayve launched supervised autonomous ride-hailing services in London, matching passengers with electric vehicles equipped with Wayve's AI Driver technology. The vehicles initially operated with licensed safety drivers onboard, following global restructuring plans that included cutting about 3,300 jobs. Isiaka Agbaje, 42, a cab driver at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos, said the ride-hailing business no longer pays his bills.

The move redirected savings and investments into autonomous vehicles and robotaxi partnerships, and Uber did not officially link its exit from the Nigerian market to investment in AI efficiency. Premium Times gathered responses from nearly a dozen cab drivers operating in Lagos, Nigeria's commercial nerve centre, Abuja and other parts of the country. Samuel Adeoti put Uber's commission at 35 per cent and gave a hypothetical example of a ₦10,000 trip, from which he said Uber deducted ₦3,500, leaving ₦6,500 with the driver. After spending about ₦5,000 on fuel, he said a driver would have just ₦1,500 left to cover other costs including car maintenance and dealings with the task force, police and road safety. In 2023, shortly after being sworn in, President Bola Tinubu introduced sweeping reforms in Nigeria's foreign exchange market and the downstream petroleum sector, abolishing what the government termed a wasteful subsidy regime and harmonising the foreign exchange market.

Lanre Mustapha, an ex-Uber driver, said the company failed to adequately address drivers' complaints about fares and commissions amid sky-high domestic prices. He said drivers had protested against low fares about six months before Uber left Nigeria, but the company failed to address their concerns. Mustapha said he migrated to InDrive and described uncertainty over account suspensions there as a major challenge, saying workers can wake up to find themselves permanently blocked without stated reasons. John Promise, 39, another driver on the platform, said drivers remained because they had no better options and did not want to lose access to their customers. Innocent Ogwuche, another ex-Uber driver, said he initially had a positive experience because of the app and safety features, but things changed when fuel prices increased and automated fares failed to keep pace with operating costs.

Ogwuche said Uber is not the one fuelling the car or doing the maintenance, and he lamented inadequate compensation for trips delayed by traffic. He said he repeatedly faced technical problems while accessing his driver account, which contributed to his decision to leave the platform. Abubakar Aliyu, a cab driver based in Abuja, said a union, the Amalgamated Union of App-Based Transport Workers of Nigeria (AUTTWON), represents ride-hailing and app-based transport drivers such as those on Bolt and InDrive. He said the union uses strikes, fare boycotts and court actions to push back against algorithmic control, but platforms often treat workers as independent contractors rather than employees. Aliyu said platforms use legal technicalities and grey areas to avoid collective bargaining agreements and demands for better service conditions, adding that the union is engaging rather slowly and faces challenges.

Earlier this year, the World Bank released a report titled World Development Report 2026: The Promise of Artificial Intelligence, which assesses how AI impacts 5.6 billion people in low- and middle-income countries. The report showed that AI offers a rare path to accelerate growth at a time when global development progress has dipped to its weakest pace in 75 years, and it can help bridge chronic gaps in health, agricultural guidance for farmers and basic administrative support for governments. It urged policymakers to follow a structured three-step approach: adopt existing AI tools, tailor the tools to local realities and develop the technology. The report cautioned that traditional work faces targeted white-collar disruption, entry-level hiring freezes and widening productivity gaps, and it warned that economic benefits from AI tend to flow toward business and capital owners rather than wage workers. It said mass automation is less immediate in developing economies, where only 4.5 per cent of jobs are highly exposed compared to 14.2 per cent in wealthy nations.

On 22 October, Uber announced a separate expansion of its AI adoption, making ChatGPT Work available to more than 30,000 employees globally after an initial pilot involving 1,000 workers. Through initiatives like Uber AI Solutions and Digital Tasks, Uber also lets drivers and contractors earn money by labelling data, recording voice prompts and evaluating AI responses during downtime. Digital labour sociologist Antonio Casilli describes this move as a "Great Digital Labour Convergence", adding that merging physical gig work with micro-task data labelling normalises underpaid, algorithmically managed work across more industries while threatening traditional employment protections. He argued that platforms serve as testing grounds where industrialists experiment with ideas they plan to roll out across all labour markets, and that even traditionally stable professions have begun to absorb gig-like features such as flexible scheduling, task-based pay, algorithmic oversight and precarious autonomy. In their book, 'Notes Towards a Digital Worker's Enquiry', Julie Chen, a professor of communications and digital labour, and other scholars examined how previously viewed "unorganizable" digital and precarious workforces are building collective resistance and identifying tactical chokepoints within platform capitalism.

stories.Headline: Hong Kong companies and family offices invest in AI financial analyst ARTi
stories.Summary:
An AI financial analyst named ARTi launched in July to provide investment research. Hong Kong listed companies and family offices made strategic investments in the startup. The product was incubated from a family office business system in Hong Kong. It allows users to inquire about stock trends and quotes via chat. The tool can also generate investment research reports for its users.

Delin Holdings, listed as 1709.HK, made a strategic investment in the platform. C Capital provided 1.5 million US dollars in Pre-A round funding in June. This investment gave the company a pre-money valuation of 30 million US dollars. The product reached 70,000 users within four months of its official launch. It connects to communication platforms like WhatsApp instead of requiring a new App.

CEO Eason Zhang said the tool solves the problem of information overload. He stated that every investment judgment made by the AI must be verifiable. Zhang believes professional agents need specific data sources and financial analysis frameworks. He noted that general large models often prefer guessing over admitting uncertainty. The team uses multi-model collaboration to establish a system for result verification.

High-net-worth investors and beginners, including Hong Kong university students, use the service. Some users from Delin's wealth management business provide core customer feedback. These professional investors require continuous tracking and clear frameworks for their research. Many users have expressed a willingness to pay for these professional services. The product currently serves as a value-added service for certain high-net-worth clients.

Eason Zhang previously served as a strategic consulting partner at a global firm. He founded a fintech enterprise after leaving that consulting role in 2015. The startup combines Silicon Valley AI technology with Hong Kong financial business resources. CTO Steve brings experience from Silicon Valley entrepreneurship to the technical architecture. A chief scientist from a Silicon Valley laboratory serves as an expert consultant.

The company has started its Series A financing to grow the business. ARTi plans to launch a subscription model with various monthly paid packages. These tiers are designed at 20, 100, and 200 US dollars per month. Paid users will gain access to virtual trading functions and research services. The articles leave open when large-scale charging will officially begin for users.

stories.Headline: Air Marshal Tejinder Singh highlights AI's role in future military capabilities at Pune seminar
stories.Summary:
Air Marshal Tejinder Singh, the Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee, spoke about the strategic importance of Artificial Intelligence in shaping future military capabilities and operational preparedness, according to a Defence Ministry official. He made his remarks at a seminar held as part of a three-day Capsule on Science, Technology and Applied Research Programme at the Military Institute of Technology in Pune. The seminar carried the theme of AI versus AI as a new frontier of warfare and brought together tri-service leadership along with technology experts from academia and industry. Those present deliberated on the changing character of warfare in the AI era, the Integrated Defence Staff Headquarters said in a post on the social media platform X. The seminar included sessions by subject matter experts from the Armed Forces, academia and industry that covered emerging AI technologies, Sovereign AI, AI-enabled weapon systems, autonomous and counter-autonomous systems, human-machine teaming and decision superiority in multi-domain operations.

A key highlight was an event called Navonmesh, described as a meeting place for innovation and new ideas, where leading industry partners showcased cutting-edge AI technologies and innovative solutions along with their potential military applications. The seminar reinforced the importance of jointness, indigenous technological capabilities and collaboration between the Armed Forces, academia and industry in preparing for the evolving challenges of future warfare. Before the seminar, Air Marshal Tejinder Singh visited the National Defence Academy at Khadakwasla in Pune, where he reviewed key training infrastructure, the curriculum and forthcoming development projects aimed at further enhancing the training environment. The Integrated Defence Staff Headquarters said he also visited the outdoor tactical training site and interacted with cadets undergoing camp training, gaining insights into their training experiences and professional development. Addressing the cadets, he urged them to uphold the highest traditions of military ethos and to imbibe the core values of discipline, integrity and dedication while fostering a spirit of jointness.

He further urged them to strive for professional excellence and to prepare themselves to shoulder future responsibilities, carrying forward the legacy of what the statement called a distinguished cradle of military leadership. In a separate message, the Indian Air Force said on X that a exercise named AJHE26 was set to commence at Air Force Station Jamnagar from November 17 to 19, 2026. That exercise will bring together the Indian Defence Forces, the National Disaster Management Authority, the Indian Coast Guard and friendly foreign countries, according to the Indian Air Force message. The stated aim of the exercise is to strengthen joint preparedness and coordination in disaster response among the participating forces and agencies. The articles do not say what decisions, if any, followed from the seminar or the academy visit, and they give no further details on the outcomes of either.

stories.Headline: Higgsfield releases AI Ad Generator for small businesses to create video adverts without studios
stories.Summary:
Higgsfield released an AI Ad Generator for small businesses to create video adverts without using studios. This software allows owners to produce short clips for social media using only a web browser. The tool was highlighted in a report published on 13 November 2026. It targets business owners in cities like Harare, Bulawayo, and Mutare. The system turns product links or photos into finished video advertisements.

The tool requires a product link or up to five uploaded images to build a profile. Users can choose from over 40 ready to use avatars or describe a custom one. It offers nine ad modes, including UGC, Tutorial, Product Review, Unboxing, TV Spot, and Hyper Motion. Other modes include UGC Virtual Try On, Pro Virtual Try On, and a Wild Card option. Seedance 2.0 provides native audio and lip sync in 9:16, 16:9, and 1:1 shapes.

Higgsfield states that the tool writes the script, directs the shots, and delivers the final cut. The company claims a business can go from a product link to a video in two minutes. They say the generator removes the need for filming, a crew, and post production. No design or editing experience is required to use the creative suite. The software supports multiple languages, though English is the default setting for the avatars.

Small businesses in Zimbabwe are affected because traditional production is often too expensive for them. These firms often lack the budget for cameras, presenters, locations, editors, and professional crews. Many owners also lack the specific skills needed for writing scripts, lighting, and cutting video. Consequently, many small firms rely on a single photo and a caption for their marketing. Video is now the format that customers expect for products like clothes and hardware.

Interest in these tools follows the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy launched in March 2026. The Zimbabwean government urged the private sector to invest in technology and partner with start ups. The government also planned to offer incentives to businesses that integrate AI into their operations. This strategy encouraged companies to use AI for practical purposes like marketing to see quick benefits. AI tools aim to close the gap for firms that cannot afford professional agencies.

Users must now test the tool with their own products to verify the vendor claims. Business owners should check if the generated voices sound credible to their specific local audiences. They must also ensure that prices and measures are shown as their customers expect. The articles leave the specific pricing plans for the Higgsfield service open and unstated. It remains for users to verify which specific languages are supported beyond the default English.

stories.Headline: New Jersey governor Mikie Sherrill pushes state action on child safety and Big Tech privacy
stories.Summary:
New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill spoke with Nilay Patel on November 16, 2026, about recent midterms and tech policy. Sherrill believes her own election served as a preview for the huge Democratic victories seen in those recent midterm races. She started her campaign in November 2024, immediately after Donald Trump won the presidential election in that same month. The governor focused her campaign on the dual themes of accountability and affordability to connect with the voting public. She believes the Democratic Party is most powerful when it fights for working families through these specific policy goals.

The governor is now exercising state power to address child safety and Big Tech overreach because federal regulation is lacking. She is leading fights regarding online privacy, age verification, and data centers while also expecting more litigation against Big Tech. Sherrill mentioned a Meta settlement and the privacy implications of AI and Flock, which she believes require more public discussion. In India, Parliament enacted the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, to create a framework for protecting personal information. The Supreme Court of India previously recognized privacy as a fundamental right in the 2017 Justice K.S. Puttaswamy case.

Governor Sherrill stated that she feels fantastic about the midterms and believes New Jersey acted as a political bellwether. She said that voters were furious and wanted a leader to address the fear caused by Elon Musk's actions. Sherrill argued that corruption is tied to people's pocketbooks, citing Trump's alleged profits from an Iranian war and Russian diesel. She believes that being a strong leader requires being accountable and honest about government problems rather than sweeping them away. The governor also noted that the current era of politics makes it nearly impossible to hide information from people.

Nilay Patel noted that corruption appeared as a top issue in a Guardian poll and linked it to tech billionaires. He mentioned that influencer politics is rising, citing New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Abdul El-Sayed as key examples. The House Oversight Committee also used a hype reel style video to communicate, which Patel described as being incredibly effective. In Jammu and Kashmir, citizens using digital platforms for banking and education are affected by data collection and processing. These individuals leave digital trails including telephone numbers, locations, and financial details that can reveal intimate aspects of their lives.

Sherrill observed that voters were angry about tech billionaires who flip-flop between liberal and Trump values just to make money. She mentioned that Trump allegedly received payments from the UAE to open floodgates for high-end semiconductor chips despite Congress. The governor also discovered that the previous administration failed to clear non-citizens off the voter rolls in New Jersey. In India, the DPDP Act has sparked a debate over whether the law protects citizens or enables state surveillance. The region of Jammu and Kashmir has a specific history with internet restrictions that makes these digital rights very significant.

The Supreme Court of India will soon consider the DNPA challenge to clarify the relationship between privacy and freedom of expression. This legal process will determine if data protection can exist without weakening accountability or restricting the freedom of the press. Sherrill believes that being present on social media is a permanent fixture for politicians who want to reach the public. The articles leave open whether the DPDP Act can truly safeguard citizens against excessive governmental access to their personal data. It remains unclear if the new brand of influencer politics will continue to wield algorithms against their own corporate owners.

stories.Headline: VT Markets launches a ChatGPT and Claude plugin for real-time asset tracking

VT Markets, a multi-asset broker, announced on November 17, 2026 the launch of its official plugin for ChatGPT and Claude, which brings real-time asset tracking and economic intelligence directly into the conversational AI platforms. The integration lets traders, investors and market observers analyse global assets without leaving their chat interface or switching between financial dashboards. The plugin provides data and visual analytics across forex, commodities, global indices and equities, and users can surface price movements, highlight top gainers and losers, track market sentiment and generate visual charts on demand. It also lets users check upcoming central bank decisions and corporate earnings schedules so they can prepare for potential price movements ahead of major market shifts. The announcement was issued from Sydney through PR Newswire.

The plugin's listed features include multi-asset access across forex, commodities, global indices and equities, instant display of price action charts, top gainers and losers and broad market sentiment, live tracking of upcoming macroeconomic announcements and corporate earnings, and conversion of simple conversational queries into structured market summaries. VT Markets said the integration puts market intelligence where daily research happens and removes friction from financial analysis, equipping market participants worldwide to evaluate global assets, track macro trends and turn raw data into actionable insights instantly. Looking ahead, the company plans to roll out secure account connectivity for the plugins, which would allow traders to view their portfolios and prepare orders directly within the chat. The articles give no further dates for that rollout.

VT Markets is the company behind the plugin and describes itself as a leading multi-asset broker. The articles do not name any individual executive or give any personal statement beyond the company's description of the launch. VT Markets included a disclaimer stating that it does not represent the material as accurate, current or complete and that the information should not be relied upon as such. The disclaimer also says the information comes from a third party and is not a recommendation, an offer to buy or sell, or a solicitation to participate in any trading strategy, and it advises readers to seek their own advice. It adds that AI-generated content is for informational purposes only and does not constitute financial or investment advice.

The context given is that the plugin is designed to streamline daily research by placing market data inside the chat tools people already use. stories.Headline: Apple asks developers to build Siri integrations for its 2027 smart glasses
stories.Summary:
Apple plans to lean heavily on Siri AI for its smart glasses, according to a Bloomberg report by Mark Gurman, published in Sunday's "Power On" newsletter and covered by Gizmodo on November 16, 2026, and AppleInsider on November 15, 2026. Apple wants to challenge Meta's Muse AI by giving its smart glasses smoother agentic capabilities, specifically tighter integrations with third-party apps that Siri can control. Gurman reported that Apple expects app developers to prepare for the eventual introduction of its smart glasses in 2027. Apple's long-rumored smart glasses are expected to lean on AI processing for its first release. The way the glasses function with AI will be key to their success, according to AppleInsider.

Apple wants developers to focus on Siri integrations rather than having apps running fully on the glasses, so specific functions within apps are accessible to Siri and can be called upon by users wearing the glasses. Because the Siri integrations are being developed for the iPhone first, software makers won't need to build separate applications for the glasses. Developers will be able to make specific functions within their existing apps accessible to Siri, allowing users to complete tasks through voice commands without opening or navigating the apps themselves. Apple's approach is similar to the rollout of HomeView, a device that does not allow third-party apps to run directly but lets apps with existing CarPlay support play audio and video. Apple is also looking into integrations with Starbucks that could let you order a drink with the Siri AI voice assistant on its smart glasses, shop through Amazon, and book movie tickets through Fandango.

The thinking inside Apple is that while Meta has the increasingly popular Muse agent, Apple has the App Store, according to Gurman. Apple believes it has the upper hand on current market dominator Meta, with its advantage coming from its pool of developers. Apple has a much larger pool of developers at its disposal in the App Store and worked on Siri integrations for the iPhone long beforehand, so there should be little effort needed to make those Siri integrations work with the smart glasses. Apple is making a similar plea to developers to work on those elements before the launch of the Apple Vision Pro. With any luck, it should launch with a robust and vast number of things you can call upon Siri to do, without waiting for developers to catch up.

Among the rumored agentic capabilities are using your voice to have Siri AI order you a car through Uber or book you a reservation at a restaurant through OpenTable. Meta has the same vision for Muse, which already lives on its smart glasses, but Apple hopes its more tight-knit relationship with developers will make app integrations easier. Bloomberg notes that Apple's advantage isn't unique, because Samsung's and Google's relationships with developers through Google's Android XR platform are equally as established and could offer the same opportunities. Meta's Muse has found ways to offer agentic capabilities through web browsers as opposed to specific apps.

Whether Apple has bright ideas on solving increasing privacy concerns or convincing people that smart glasses aren't a bad idea in general remains to be seen. Meta popularized the modern-day template for what smart glasses are, and Samsung and Google now have their own equivalent in a recently launched lineup of "intelligent eyewear." For a device like smart glasses, leaning on Siri integrations makes sense, especially if Apple keeps to its plan of making thin and light smart spectacles, because it won't have enough onboard processing available to handle much in the way of apps. CarPlay and Siri AI solve that by pushing the hard work to a nearby iPhone.

Apple's smart glasses will work with apps, but probably through Siri AI, in a similar way to the CarPlay-like HomeView. Apple's plan for its AI-equipped smart glasses is to lean on integrations with a user's existing iPhone apps. Apple is expecting app developers to prepare for the eventual introduction of its smart glasses in 2027, and the Siri integrations are being developed for the iPhone first. Whether Apple has any bright ideas on solving increasing privacy concerns or convincing people that smart glasses aren't a bad idea in general remains to be seen.

stories.Headline: Future Caribbean names Caribbean Grid AI, Neptune Analytics and Miracle as top startups at NYSE showcase
stories.Summary:
Future Caribbean named Caribbean Grid AI, Neptune Analytics and Miracle as the standout companies of its investor showcase at the New York Stock Exchange on Friday evening, November 13, 2026. The event was co-hosted by Future Caribbean founder Lily Dash, with Silicon Valley venture capitalist Bill Tai joining virtually. The invitation-only evening brought 16 finalist founder teams before investors, family offices, diplomats and enterprise leaders. The showcase was the final stage of a programme launched in May at IDB Invest Sustainability Week in Barbados. More than 450 builders from 39 countries took part, with finalists selected through more than 2,000 reviews and over 600 one-to-one advisory sessions.

The programme was supported by a network of more than 200 advisors and judges and more than 48 partner organizations. The evening opened with remarks from Brian Baumann, Global Head of Technology Ecosystems at the NYSE, followed by a virtual address from Minister Williams. Williams noted that 56 Jamaican builders took part in the programme and eight Jamaican teams reached the finals. The showcase was supported by sponsors Andrik Capital, Invest Barbados and Polymath Research, event partner Lingnum Security Limited, and Book Better as official travel sponsor. The programme itself ran on Buildathon-in-a-Box, Future Caribbean's agentic platform, which coordinated around 1,200 participants and more than 600 one-to-one advisory calls.

Fayval Williams, Jamaica's Minister of Finance and the Public Service, told the room that the Caribbean should not watch the AI transformation happen but help shape it. Williams told the finalists, "You made us proud. Extremely proud." She said the companies show that when you build carefully, for real users and to last, a solution that makes it in the Caribbean can make it anywhere. She said Jamaica wants to work with serious partners on practical problems like these.

Lily Dash, Founder of Future Caribbean, said Caribbean founders showed investors, diplomats and enterprise leaders at the New York Stock Exchange that category-defining companies can come from anywhere. Dash said the winners stood out, but every team on that stage is building technology that solves real problems at home and can serve customers around the world. She said Future Caribbean is now focused on turning these conversations into investment, partnerships and revenue. Bill Tai described how a single Caribbean nation can serve as a testbed to get a product running before it is replicated across the region. He pointed to a moment when agentic AI is allowing companies with a handful of employees to build at global scale.

Senior diplomatic and institutional leaders in attendance included Aubrey Webson, Antigua and Barbuda's Ambassador to the United Nations, and Oliver Mair, Jamaica's Consul General in New York. Representatives of the Consulate General of The Bahamas, Invest Barbados and UNDP also attended. On the investor side, Brian Feuer, former Global Head of Portfolio Management at McKinsey, was joined by Steven Grin of Lateral Frontiers VC, Krishna Singh of GTCapital and Sergio Fernández de Córdova, Chairman of the PVBLIC Foundation. Intel was represented by Managing Director Mark Castleman and NVIDIA by Principal Solutions Architect Anton Alexander and scientist Camir Ricketts. OCEANIX co-founder and CEO Itai Madamombe and World Identity Network founder Mariana Dahan, who previously led the World Bank's Identification for Development agenda, brought expertise in ocean infrastructure and digital identity.

Cultural figures in the room ranged from Barbadian singer-songwriter JusJay to Shelley Worrell, founder of Brooklyn's Little Caribbean. Two of the three winners are tackling the Caribbean's energy problem, while the third is taking on one of its most stretched health services. When Barbados Light & Power set Caribbean Grid AI a forecasting challenge, the Barbados-based team beat the utility's benchmark by 12%. Founded by data analyst Andrew Narine, the platform draws on ten years of local solar and wind data to help grid operators decide when to store, dispatch, hold or curtail renewable power. The utility is now reviewing it as Barbados works toward its renewable energy targets.

Caribbean power producers spend around US$8.5 billion a year on imported fuel, and roughly US$4 billion of it escapes as waste heat. Trinidad and Tobago's Neptune Analytics, founded by Simon Neptune, is turning that loss into electricity by capturing heat from sources as low as 60°C, well below the 200°C most existing systems require. The company has already secured a non-binding letter of intent for 20 megawatts of capacity at a power plant in Tobago. Miracle began with an injury: occupational therapist Brenda Luo hurt her hand and could not get therapy at her local clinic. Her answer turns an ordinary mirror into an AR-guided, AI-coached rehab session that flags pain and logs progress for clinicians.

Early testing in Alberta recorded 100% task completion at one site, and for the Caribbean, where rehab specialists are scarce, it means a single therapist can support far more patients at home. All three winners will walk away with consulting hours from EY-Parthenon, giving them access to one of the world's leading strategy advisory teams as they take their products to market. Jamaica's Project Lighthouse, co-founded by Sammarieo Brown, is building a relief platform backed by a catastrophe bond that would pay citizens directly rather than routing funds through government. Field Watch AI, founded by Onassis Nottage, proposed a satellite and sensor pilot to monitor hurricane shelters in The Bahamas in real time.

Moon Trades Technologies is applying its mapping technology to disaster coordination, and Sovereign Nature Intelligence is using AI agents to speed up verification of blue carbon credits. Dataffluent, led by Raquel Seville in Kingston, uses AI agents to assess the small businesses banks typically turn away. WAM Connect moves Trinidad and Tobago, Barbados, Jamaican and Guyanese dollars between islands in seconds instead of routing them through US correspondent banks. NATIVE gives founders anywhere a single account to bank and run their company, and Yadli lets diaspora families verify building work on homes in Jamaica before any payment is released.

FlowStay, which recently went live at its first hotel in California, is bringing AI concierge services to Caribbean properties, while Verocitu's Pulse turns local radio broadcasts into searchable intelligence for AI travel assistants. Wellnest uses AI to triage patients and draft clinical notes in Jamaican clinics, including in Patois, and Harvest pools orders from small farms so local produce can reach hotels and supermarkets. Future Caribbean's commercialization phase, delivered in partnership with ACTAI Advisors, will now focus on helping showcase companies turn investor and enterprise interest into funding, pilots and partnerships. Founders also recorded interviews with NYSE Wired, the exchange's technology media franchise, extending their reach to a global audience.

Future Caribbean's MOU with the PVBLIC Foundation will connect founders with investment and technology transfer frameworks across Small Island Developing States. Future Caribbean is exploring its next buildathon and investor showcase to bring more founders into the programme. The articles leave open which companies will secure funding, pilots or partnerships from the conversations at the showcase. The articles also leave open the date of the next buildathon and investor showcase.

stories.Headline: BlackLine unveils agentic finance platform with governance console and Databricks connectivity
stories.Summary:
BlackLine, Inc. (Nasdaq: BL) unveiled a series of platform innovations at BeyondTheBlack 2026 in Orlando, Florida, on Nov. 17, 2026, according to a GlobeNewswire release dated the same day. The release said the innovations span next-generation platform architecture, Record-to-Report, and Invoice-to-Cash. BlackLine described the advancements as a shift for the Office of the CFO away from fragmented, task-level automation toward full-scale, governed financial orchestration. The release said enterprises accelerating AI adoption face the challenge of scaling agentic execution across complex financial workflows without compromising deterministic accuracy, auditability, or governance. BlackLine said it built the platform on more than 25 years of financial process expertise.

The release said the platform unifies financial data, core applications, and specialized AI agents into an orchestrated digital workforce. It introduced a Finance Control Console, described as a centralized governance, policy-enforcement, and observability command center giving real-time visibility into agent actions, enforcing deterministic guardrails, enabling human-in-the-loop approvals, and guaranteeing auditability. It introduced Agentic Orchestration, a coordination engine connecting AI agents and financial processes into multi-step workflows that merge autonomous execution with enterprise financial logic and compliance policies. It introduced a Unified Data Foundation and Verity Integrate, an enterprise data architecture connecting financial data, ERPs, and applications, plus Agent-Ready Connectivity via open standards including the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The release said BlackLine introduced native connectivity with Databricks, with Databricks OpenSharing letting customers share governed data without duplicating data or building complex pipelines, and said Verity Accruals is built on Databricks using the Databricks Partner Well-Architected Framework.

Jeremy Ung, Chief Technology Officer at BlackLine, said the true measure of AI in finance is not simply what it can calculate but what an enterprise can trust it to execute autonomously. Ung said BlackLine is delivering a trusted digital workforce for the Office of the CFO. He said combining intelligent agents with deep financial expertise and deterministic controls is transforming how financial work gets done. He said this frees finance leaders from manual process management to steer strategic business outcomes. Sarah Branfman, Global Vice President, ISV at Databricks, said customers shouldn't have to choose between control over their data and speed to value.

Branfman said that with BlackLine they don't have to, and that through OpenSharing customers share governed data between BlackLine and their lakehouse without copying it or building pipelines. She said Verity Accruals built on Databricks delivers AI-native finance automation on the platform enterprises already trust with their data. Christopher Giambra, Senior Manager of Corporate Accounting at Delaware North, said his company trusts BlackLine more than anybody else in the business and that trust is paramount when it comes to AI. Giambra said deploying Verity Prepare has fundamentally elevated reconciliation workflows and that expanding into Verity Match across high-volume treasury and credit card operations will be transformative. The release said Delaware North, a global hospitality and entertainment leader, is already putting the agentic innovations to work.

The release said BlackLine brought consolidation and financial close together into an integrated, high-velocity Record-to-Report engine, with Financial Consolidation taking an AI-native approach that unifies enterprise financial close and consolidation in a single connected workflow. It said Autonomous Close advances toward a touchless close through Agentic Reconciliations, Verity Score, and Verity Retrieve, automating reconciliation cycles, benchmarking reconciliation quality and audit readiness, and retrieving supporting documentation while preserving human oversight. It said Verity Match applies machine intelligence to high-volume transaction matching, isolating true exceptions so accounting teams focus on items requiring complex analytical judgment. The release said BlackLine expanded agentic capabilities across the receivables lifecycle, building on the commercial momentum and general availability of Verity Collect and Verity Remit. The release said approximately 4,300 customers across multiple industries partner with BlackLine.

The release said the innovations address a time when trust is on the line, combining agentic execution with the accuracy, control, and oversight finance demands. It said BlackLine is turning trust into a catalyst for transformation, empowering finance teams to confidently scale AI and drive better business outcomes. It said the BlackLine Agentic Financial Operations Platform, powered by Verity AI, is where the Office of the CFO scales AI across Record-to-Report, Invoice-to-Cash, and the processes where finance owns the controls. It said BlackLine is supported by industry-leading R&D investment and world-class security practices. It directed readers to www.BlackLine.com to explore the platform and the innovations unveiled at BeyondTheBlack 2026.

The release listed Invoice-to-Cash innovations including Credit & Risk Management for AI-powered credit scoring, underwriting, and portfolio risk monitoring, Customer Onboarding for streamlined customer evaluation and account setup through connected digital workflows, and Disputes & Deductions for automated dispute intake, classification, and investigation. It also listed a Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) Agent that analyzes payment trends, predicts collection bottlenecks, and prescribes prioritized intervention strategies to compress cash conversion cycles. A separate KPMG Azerbaijan interview with Tural Jahangirov, Manager at KPMG Azerbaijan, dated Nov. 14, 2026, said the role of tax within a business is expanding beyond calculations and compliance. The interview said understanding the financial impact of tax decisions, maintaining data consistency, and identifying potential risks early are becoming increasingly important. It said technology should complement, rather than replace, professional judgement in tax decision-making.

stories.Headline: TARSBOT and Aptiv partner to develop and scale industrial embodied AI robots for smart manufacturing
stories.Summary:
TARSBOT and Aptiv signed an agreement to deepen their strategic collaboration in embodied AI on November 16, 2026. This event took place in Shanghai during the 9th China International Import Expo. The two companies are partnering to develop and scale industrial robots for smart manufacturing. They aim to connect robotic systems with operational applications in real world environments. This signing marks a more systematic and scaled phase of their existing cooperation.

Aptiv expects to deploy 100 TARSBOT A-Series robots by the end of 2026 across 8 process categories. These robots will cover 33 application scenarios, including production management, coordinated inspection, and flexible assembly. The parties plan to achieve mass production in 2026 using high performance computing platforms. A target scale of 1,000 units is set for China's first industrial embodied AI robot fleet. The first phase is currently being implemented at an Aptiv production site.

The two companies are responsible for validating applications in real industrial environments to support iterative development. They stated that insights from production will help develop the AWE general purpose foundation model. TARSBOT provides end to end embodied AI capabilities and experience in real production line applications. Aptiv contributes established engineering expertise, rigorous standards, and intelligent power distribution solutions. These combined efforts aim to support efficient and reliable deployment at scale.

Manufacturers worldwide are affected as they face growing demand for intelligent automation and greater supply chain efficiency. The collaboration aims to demonstrate that scalable deployment can be validated in practical industrial settings. Embodied AI is emerging as an important force in advancing next generation productivity for these manufacturers. The project provides a validated industrial reference for replicating AI across additional scenarios. This creates broader opportunities for smart manufacturing on a global scale.

The Jiading District Government of Shanghai provided support for the development of the industrial robot fleet. A first batch of robots has already entered operation at an Aptiv smart factory. High performance computing platforms provide reliable compute for motion control, perception, and decision making. The collaboration builds on the rich real world manufacturing environments found within China. These platforms support highly reliable operation in real industrial settings.

TARSBOT and Aptiv will continue to validate their robotic applications in real industrial environments. They will further integrate intelligent power distribution solutions into the TARSBOT embodied AI robots. The companies will work to expand embodied AI across additional manufacturing scenarios worldwide. The articles do not state the specific timeline for the 1,000 unit target. They leave open the exact date for the completion of the mass production phase.

stories.Headline: Marsh's Schnur links AI tools to a doubling of client cyber incidents
stories.Summary:
Marsh reported that its clients filed 105 cyber incidents in the last two weeks of October, which is more than double the 48 incidents recorded in the final two weeks of May, according to data the insurance broker released and Reuters reported on November 17, 2026. Meredith Schnur, who leads the US and Canada cyber practice at Marsh Risk, told Reuters in an interview this week that attackers are using AI enabled and agentic tools to identify vulnerabilities, and she said AI could be attributed to a significant number of the incidents. She said the speed and scale of AI tool adoption, combined with organizations taking longer to contain attacks and respond to incidents, were the main factors driving the recent increase in cyber incident volumes. Schnur said AI is not a peril but an amplification of risk in all areas, and she said the technology lets attackers find and exploit longstanding vulnerabilities such as unpatched software, exposed systems and weak identity controls at a much faster pace.

The rise in reported incidents requires businesses and their insurers to contend with attacks that spread faster and reach more targets, because AI tools that are becoming more widely accessible let attackers scale their operations with fewer resources. GlobalData expects global cyber insurance premiums to rise 6.9% to $16.6 billion in 2026, before growth accelerates to 10% in 2027 to reach $18.3 billion, as businesses respond to rising attack frequency. The Marsh figures compare the final two weeks of October with the final two weeks of May, and the 105 incidents more than double the 48 recorded in the earlier period. The report ties the increase to AI adoption and to slower containment and response times, and it says the wider availability of AI tools is widening the pool of potential targets and putting pressure on businesses.

Schnur, the US and Canada cyber practice leader at Marsh Risk, is the person the articles identify as explaining the data, and she attributed a significant share of the incidents to AI in her interview with Reuters this week. She said the signs that attackers are using AI enabled and agentic tools to identify vulnerabilities are happening, and she described AI as an amplification of risk in all areas rather than a peril in itself. She said the speed and scale of AI tool adoption, together with organizations taking longer to contain attacks and respond to incidents, were the main factors behind the recent increase in cyber incident volumes. The reporting was by Noor Zainab Hussain and Manya Saini in Bengaluru, with editing by Shilpi Majumdar, and the story was published by Reuters and carried by Insurance Journal.

The context the articles give is a cyber insurance market that GlobalData expects to grow faster over the next two years as businesses respond to rising attack frequency, with premiums reaching $16.6 billion in 2026 and $18.3 billion in 2027. The articles do not say what Marsh or insurers will change in response to the data, and they do not describe any new policy terms or claims figures beyond the incident counts and the premium forecasts. What happens next, according to the articles, is continued growth in cyber insurance premiums at a faster pace over the next two years, driven by the rising frequency of attacks that the Marsh data shows.

stories.Headline: Fluke study finds 78 percent of data center operators hit electrical disruption in past year
stories.Summary:
Fluke Corporation published a study on November 17, 2026, finding that 78 percent of data center operators experienced electrical or power-system issues contributing to disruption, delays, downtime or serious near-misses in the past year. The study was announced from Everett, Washington, and distributed by GlobeNewswire. Fluke said the global race to build and expand AI data centers could face a major setback. The research raised questions about whether the infrastructure behind the AI boom can deliver on the industry's ambitious growth plans. Operators are racing to secure additional grid capacity while weaknesses inside data centers threaten to delay new AI workloads and disrupt existing operations.

Only 33 percent of operators say their electrical infrastructure is fully ready for higher-density AI workloads. 34 percent say electrical skills shortages have delayed infrastructure upgrades or new capacity. 29 percent say power-quality issues have reduced their ability to deploy or operate AI/GPU workloads. 29 percent report that electrical problems are only identified after performance or equipment failure, or downtime, has occurred. Fewer than half of operators, 45 percent, report real-time visibility across critical electrical systems.

Parker Burke, President of Fluke Corporation, said the industry has spent years asking where the power will come from. He said the findings show the focus should also be on how effectively data centers can use the power they already have. He said the electrical infrastructure inside data centers is becoming a critical bottleneck as AI drives unprecedented demand for computing capacity. He said that without addressing this last-mile challenge, the industry risks having the power to expand but not the infrastructure to deliver. Burke also said grid constraints are largely outside an operator's control, while what is within their control is how effectively they monitor, maintain and manage the electrical infrastructure they already have.

Six in ten operators, 60 percent, say recruiting qualified electrical technicians has become more difficult. Three-quarters of operators, 76 percent, say access to sufficient power and grid capacity is moderately or severely limiting their ability to expand. Operators report an average 12-month wait to secure additional grid connection or power capacity for AI and GPU-related expansion. The study was commissioned by Fluke on behalf of Censuswide and surveyed 1,300 data-center industry operators and professionals across six countries: the US, UK, Germany, France, India and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Censuswide is an international market research consultancy headquartered in London, with offices in New York, Dubai, Bristol and Glasgow.

Fluke Corporation was founded in 1948 and describes itself as the world leader in compact, professional electronic test tools and software for measuring and condition monitoring. Fluke customers are technicians, engineers, electricians, maintenance managers and metrologists who install, troubleshoot and maintain industrial, electrical and electronic equipment and calibration processes. The study examined the power, infrastructure and workforce challenges facing the industry as AI demand accelerates. The findings suggest the challenge is no longer simply securing power from the grid but ensuring data centers have the infrastructure and expertise to turn that power into reliable computing capacity. Burke said greater visibility into electrical systems and a proactive approach to maintenance will be increasingly important as operators look to maximize existing capacity, reduce disruption and support growing AI demand.

Fluke said data center operators can improve electrical reliability through regular electrical testing, power-quality monitoring, thermal inspections and preventive maintenance. Fluke said poor power quality can cause equipment malfunctions, overheating, unexpected shutdowns and downtime, and that voltage fluctuations, harmonics and electrical disturbances can affect the reliability of critical data center systems. Fluke said operators can help reduce the impact of electrical skills shortages by investing in technician training, standardized testing procedures and diagnostic tools that make electrical troubleshooting more efficient. Fluke said it provides electrical testing and measurement tools, power-quality analyzers, thermal imaging cameras and condition-monitoring solutions for data center environments. The articles leave open which specific operators or countries accounted for the reported issues and near-misses.

stories.Headline: IBM study finds only 18% of chief AI officers control AI investment decisions
stories.Summary:
The IBM Institute for Business Value published a study on November 17, 2026, dated from Armonk, New York, finding that only 18% of surveyed Chief AI Officers have full control over AI investment decisions. The global study surveyed more than 1,600 Chief AI Officers and equivalent enterprise AI leaders. It was conducted in cooperation with Oxford Economics, which surveyed 1,667 senior executives responsible for enterprise AI strategy, governance, implementation, and value realization. Those surveyed included Chief AI Officers, Chief Data and AI Officers, Heads of AI, and equivalent AI leaders, whom the study refers to collectively as CAIOs. The survey ran from April to June 2026 across 33 geographies and 20 industries.

Just 29% of respondents say their organizations adjust decisions and resources quickly when AI performance insights identify opportunities to improve outcomes. Fewer than one-third of surveyed CAIOs say AI is reshaping the business model, including what the organization sells, how it prices, or how it captures value. While only 32% say AI is reshaping the business model, 35% say it primarily strengthens the existing model, and 26% expect it to reshape the model but have not made the necessary shifts. 48% of CAIOs say AI agents initiate and execute actions across workflows, yet 75% say governance, risk or compliance delays AI-driven action. While 73% of respondents have defined where human oversight is non-negotiable, only 61% say AI decision rights are clearly defined and consistently applied.

Joanne Wright, Senior Vice President, Transformation and Operations at IBM, writes in the study's foreword that few leaders have a broader view of how AI is creating value across the enterprise. She writes that the outcomes Chief AI Officers are accountable for often depend on decisions made by others. She says successful AI leadership requires more than technical expertise or operational oversight. She says it requires gathering evidence, influencing decisions, and measuring success. The study identifies a group of high-impact CAIOs whose organizations report stronger results.

High-impact CAIOs report that 63% of AI projects deliver measurable business outcomes, compared with 43% for all other CAIOs, and that 49% move from pilot to production, versus 33%. They scale successful initiatives enterprise-wide in eight months, compared with 13.5 months among all other CAIOs. High-impact CAIOs are nearly four times as likely to say they can quickly pause, adjust or redirect AI systems without disrupting operations, and 96% of them say AI-generated outputs can trigger actions autonomously, compared with 40% of all other CAIOs. Nearly all high-impact CAIOs say AI is embedded directly into workflows compared with 59% of all others, and 94% say they use business outcomes to determine which initiatives receive additional funding and talent and which do not. 96% of high-impact CAIOs say they stop or reduce investment in initiatives that fail to deliver, even when those initiatives have senior sponsorship, compared with 46% of others, and 95% say they reinvest AI-generated productivity gains in higher-value transformation, compared with 44% of other respondents.

Only 31% of all CAIOs say clear thresholds for stopping AI initiatives are critical to AI success, and 40% say decisions are discussed when performance insights reveal opportunities, but action is delayed. 71% of CAIOs believe their organizations risk falling behind competitors in AI transformation, and CAIOs rank workflows and business processes as the top priority for change. The findings link the stronger outcomes of high-impact CAIOs with differences in how their organizations manage AI autonomy and control, redesign business workflows, and make evidence-based investment decisions. Additional analysis examined organizational behaviors associated with stronger enterprise outcomes across governance, decision rights, workflow integration, operating-model design, value management, transformation execution, and business-model innovation. The IBM Institute for Business Value is IBM's thought leadership think tank, combining global research and performance data with expertise from industry thinkers and leading academics.

The full report is available at a link on IBM's website, and the media contact is Marisa Conway of IBM Corporate Communications. IBM describes itself as a leading provider of global hybrid cloud and AI and consulting expertise, helping clients in more than 175 countries. The articles do not say what organizations should do in response to the findings, beyond the report link. They do not give the names of any surveyed CAIOs or the identities of the high-impact group. They do not break the results down by geography or industry, though the survey covered 33 geographies and 20 industries.
