stories.Headline: Kotozna secures two Japanese patents for conversational AI on its 10th anniversary
stories.Summary:
Kotozna Inc., a Tokyo-based B2B SaaS company led by CEO Genri Goto, announced on November 17, 2026, that it had secured two Japanese patents for its conversational AI technology. The announcement coincided with the company's 10th anniversary, marking a decade of work in multilingual communication and enterprise AI. Kotozna was founded in October 2016 with a mission to overcome language barriers, and it has since expanded from multilingual communication services to generative AI-powered digital concierges, enterprise chatbots and interactive AI avatars. Its solutions now provide customer assistance around the clock in more than 50 languages, which reduces repetitive staff inquiries. The two patents are JP 7898212, called a Prompt Creation System, and JP 7932206, called an Answer Generation System, and together they cover prompt optimization and knowledge retrieval.

Rather than sending large amounts of information to AI models for every question, the technology builds optimized prompts containing only the information needed to generate appropriate responses. Unlike conventional RAG systems that divide documents into fixed-length segments, Kotozna's approach organizes information into meaningful sections so that important context is preserved. The company says this reduces unnecessary processing and token consumption, which helps improve response accuracy, lower latency and optimize AI operating costs, while also supporting efficient knowledge base updates as information changes. Goto said the mission over the past ten years had stayed the same, which is to make communication easier through technology. He described the patents as an important milestone in the company's journey and as a reflection of its commitment to developing AI that is innovative, reliable and practical for businesses worldwide.

The company states that its technology addresses three critical challenges in enterprise AI adoption, namely accuracy, speed and cost efficiency, enabling businesses to deploy reliable and scalable conversational AI solutions. Kotozna's solutions are deployed at more than 500 hotels and over 50 facilities and organizations, including airports, tourism organizations, shopping malls and public institutions in Japan and overseas. As Kotozna enters its second decade, the company says it will continue advancing its conversational AI capabilities toward intelligent AI agents that can handle complex inquiries, execute tasks and automate customer service workflows. It aims to strengthen its global presence through new deployments and partnerships, bringing its AI solutions to more businesses in hospitality, tourism, retail and other sectors worldwide. Kotozna reported capital of 70,000,000 yen as of December 31, 2025, and its head office is on the third floor of Hulic JP Akasaka in Minato-ku, Tokyo.

stories.Headline: Google Cloud opens applications for a 15-week sovereign AI accelerator for European and Israeli startups
stories.Summary:
Google Cloud announced on November 17, 2026 an open call for applications to its Google for Startups Accelerator: Sovereign AI, which is available in Europe and Israel and supports startups building AI solutions for European regulatory environments. The announcement was made by Giorgia Abeltino, Head of Government Affairs and Public Policy for Google Cloud Europe, Middle East and Africa. The program is described as equity-free and runs for 15 weeks in a hybrid format with virtual and in-person sessions. Applications close on January 15, 2027, and founders can apply on the Google for Startups Accelerator page.

The accelerator is aimed at a small, high-touch cohort of late-seed to post Series A startups headquartered across Europe and Israel with strong traction that use AI for sensitive, regulated workloads. Target areas include government and public service technologies such as sovereign document processing and citizen service portals, with defense applications excluded, as well as healthcare and life sciences, regulated finance, and cybersecurity and data trust. Selected startups receive architectural mentorship, one-to-one pairing with Google Cloud engineers, and advisory support to prepare for EU AI Act Regulatory Sandboxes. Participants also get support to deploy across Google Cloud's tiered sovereign portfolio, from regional data controls and external key management to partner-operated clouds such as S3NS in France and Thales in Germany and fully air-gapped Google Distributed Cloud environments.

Abeltino wrote that artificial intelligence represents an estimated €1.2 trillion economic opportunity for Europe, and that enterprises and public institutions need advanced AI while meeting data governance requirements including the EU AI Act, NIS2, DORA, and national frameworks such as SecNumCloud and BSI's cloud security and sovereignty principles. She said the program wants founders to build in Europe with solutions made in Europe, and that digital sovereignty for startups should not mean settling for second-rate tools or lock-in to a single rigid stack. She described co-engineering with Europe's tech ecosystem so founders can scale on their own terms from day one, for instance by combining Gemini models, open-weight models like Gemma and Mistral, and verifiable data residency and cryptographic controls delivered with local European sovereign partners. Past participants, quoted in the post, said access to Google Cloud engineers who understand sovereign and regulated constraints saves young companies time and that the program helps build compliance answers into architecture from day one.

stories.Headline: South Korea pushes a health data law that lets researchers use pseudonymized medical records without patient consent
stories.Summary:
The government is pushing the Digital Healthcare Act, which would let pseudonymized medical information be used broadly without individual consent to promote medical AI development and health research, and the plan has sparked controversy. The Ministry of Health and Welfare and the National Assembly are seeking to enact the law, with passage targeted within the year, according to the 16th report. The Lee Jae Myung government had presented as a national agenda the building of an AI expressway to leap into the top three AI powers. It stated that in the bio and healthcare sectors the government would collect and link data to create a data ecosystem. Critics say the bill lowers the threshold for data use without adequate personal information safeguards.

The core of the bill is to establish a legal basis for the secondary use of personal health and medical information and to build large-scale datasets on that basis. At present, pseudonymized medical data can be used for research when individuals are hard to identify, but data collection is restricted and external transfer must be approved by the medical institutions holding the data. Under the bill, the Minister of Health and Welfare may request data provision from the National Health Insurance Service, the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service, medical data-centered hospitals and participating medical institutions. Absent special reasons, institutions that receive requests must comply. For example, if the ministry requests from Hospital A the clinical information of patients who underwent cancer surgery in a given year, the hospital must provide it in pseudonymized form unless there are special reasons not to.

A Ministry of Health and Welfare official explained that a researcher who wishes to use health and medical data must undergo review at each individual institution. The official said review criteria and procedures differ across institutions, so it often takes more than a year just to collect the data. The official also said the government has no authority to oversee whether the reviews are being conducted properly. Lee Sang-yun, chief research fellow at Research Community Health and Alternatives and an occupational and environmental medicine specialist, said that if his medical information were to be used to advance the AI industry, many people would likely not agree.

He said there is currently no consent process in place that ensures individual autonomy. Civil society groups, labor circles and patient organizations are demanding supplements, saying protections for patient rights and personal information are lacking compared with the industrial use of medical information. The data provided may include genetic information or whether the patient has a rare disease, which can allow inferences about the patient and the family disease history. Information on rare diseases with only a few dozen patients may, when combined with other information, identify an individual.

Kim Sung-Ju, head of the Korea Severe Disease Alliance, said at a National Assembly forum held on the 2nd that if research achievements based on patient information come back as high-priced pharmaceuticals or treatment technologies, the costs will again be borne by patients and the public. The current bill does not specify a right for individuals to refuse the provision of their information. The UK and Germany institutionally guarantee a patient's right not to agree to the use of their health and medical information for research and similar purposes. In England, the National Health Service operates a National Data Opt-out system that allows patients to refuse the use of their medical information for research, policymaking and similar uses.

Patients can register or withdraw their refusal at any time via the website or by phone. Another issue raised is that even if particular researchers or companies obtain industrial benefits from research using medical information, there is no structure that allows the patients who provided the information or the public to share in those benefits. The article was translated by an AI tool. More to follow.

stories.Headline: CERT-In flags low severity emBridge flaw and eMudhra removes file browsing functions to fix it
stories.Summary:
CERT-In issued a vulnerability note on November 13 about eMudhra's emBridge digital signature utility, a client-side application that lets web portals communicate with digital signature certificates and hardware tokens installed on a user's computer. The agency said the flaw could let unauthorised entities on the same local area network access file and directory names on an affected device, and it classified the threat as low severity. Cybersecurity expert Karan Saini reported the vulnerability to CERT-In. CERT-In stated that file-browsing functions within the interface did not verify whether requests came from an authorised source, and that these functions operate with the highest system privileges on Windows.

An attacker on the same local network could use a malicious webpage to send requests to emBridge and map out file and folder names on the targeted machine. The affected versions are 5.9.1.x to 5.9.3.x on Windows, 3.2.4.x to 3.2.6.x on macOS, and 3.2.0.x to 3.3.0.x on Ubuntu and Red Hat Linux. CERT-In advised users to upgrade to version 5.9.4.x or later on Windows, 3.2.7.x or later on macOS, and 3.3.1.x or later on Linux. Several government portals, including the Ministry of Corporate Affairs' MCA V3 portal, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade and the National Single Window System, rely on emBridge for DSC-based signing, and the Income Tax Department also recommends it for managing DSCs.

The agency confirmed that the flaw does not provide access to file contents, permit changes or deletions, allow code execution, or expose cryptographic keys or token PINs. eMudhra published its own advisory on the CVE and said it fixed the issue on November 11, two days before CERT-In's note, by removing the file-browsing functions from emBridge entirely. The company said that with these endpoints removed the file enumeration capability is no longer available through emBridge, and it rated the flaw's impact and risk as low. An attack would also require several conditions at once, including an affected emBridge version, a malicious webpage on the same local network, the user opening it, and a browser without Local Network Access restrictions.

The company added that its firewall and local-only request handling block direct access from other machines. Saini posted on X that while the bug was trivial, eMudhra's own advisory had further downplayed it. eMudhra told Inc42 that every digital signature certificate requires the user to enter a token PIN before use, and it pointed out that CERT-In's note confirmed keys and token PINs had not been exposed. A company spokesperson said identifying and fixing vulnerabilities is a routine part of responsible software development, and added that large global vendors like Microsoft, Oracle, Google and Adobe addressed thousands of vulnerabilities every month. The incident follows a major cybersecurity event in October where weak private keys for eMudhra's intermediate certificate authority certificates were reported.

stories.Headline: Tax accountant admits to using AI smart glasses to cheat as presidential office orders review of 528 national exams
stories.Summary:
A 34-year-old man surnamed Han admitted to using generative AI to cheat on the 2026 national tax accountant qualification exam. He turned himself in to police on Sunday and posted an apology video on YouTube on November 15. Han used AI smart glasses and a micro camera to send exam questions to a smartphone for answers. This confession prompted the presidential office to order a sweeping review of suspected AI cheating cases. The incident occurred just days before the national college entrance exam, known as the CSAT.

The review covers 528 national exams and includes the 63rd national tax accountant qualification exam where Han scored 100 in three subjects. Han earned 97.5 in public finance, while the 16,856 tax law test takers averaged 30.18 with no others above 90. The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency assigned the case to the public crime investigation team for potential business obstruction. Under Article 314 of the Criminal Act, Han faces up to five years in prison or 15 million won. The Human Resources Development Service of Korea, or HRDK, will revoke his score and file a complaint.

Ha Joon-kyung, the presidential director of national policy, convened an emergency meeting on Sunday to address the cheating. Ha stated that the Ministry of Education and other agencies must examine every possibility to prevent AI cheating. The HRDK said it would consider using radio frequency detectors and proctors dedicated to checking for AI devices. The Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants will launch a new evaluation system during practical training for apprentices. This system aims to screen out individuals who passed professional licensing exams by using cheating methods.

One tax accountant candidate called for a retest because the fairness of the exam had completely collapsed. A test taker surnamed Lee, who earned perfect LEET scores, faced online suspicion due to poor past CSAT grades. Lee previously took the CSAT five times starting in 2013 and once received a grade 7 in Korean. Other suspicions targeted three Yonsei University Mirae Campus dental hygiene graduates and candidates of the licensed customs broker exam. Suspicions also reached the certified appraiser, grade-5 national civil service, and Medical and Dental Education Eligibility tests.

Six cases of AI smart glasses cheating were caught through October in exams for gas craftsmen and various engineers. Cheating was also found in the financial investment analyst exam, the LEET, and university essay exams for early admission. Three Toeic takers and one TEPS taker were caught using AI, as were some middle and high school students. Equipment like 50,000-won micro cameras and 10,000-won earpieces are easily bought on overseas sites, including new AI pens. Critics say lax proctoring and a lack of rules on AI cheating contributed to these widespread problems.

The Education Ministry banned AI smart glasses on the CSAT, meaning violators will be barred for one year. Radio frequency detectors and revised enforcement rules banning smart glasses are not expected until the 2027 college entrance exam. The HRDK formed a task force in August and deployed 327 AI inspectors across two national qualification exams. Professor Choi Byoung-ho noted that Korea has virtually no AI cheating rules and requires a considerable budget for equipment. Professor Kim Byeong-chan suggested changing exam questions to evaluate the thought process rather than just the final result.

stories.Headline: Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin admits Korea cannot guarantee detection of AI cheating before the CSAT
stories.Summary:
Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin admitted that authorities cannot guarantee the detection of AI cheating before the college entrance exam. This admission occurred on November 16 during a National Assembly Education Committee meeting held in Yeouido, Seoul. The minister spoke during a plenary meeting while answering questions from lawmakers about the security of the upcoming test. He acknowledged that countermeasures against miniature cameras and similar equipment would probably not be perfect for the examination. These statements were made just two days before the start of the College Scholastic Ability Test in Korea.

The government will now require candidates to surrender smart devices and block public Wi-Fi at all examination centers. Authorities also announced the formation of an interagency task force to handle the threat of AI assisted cheating. These new measures were announced on November 16 to protect the integrity of the largest annual national examination. The government is also ordering a retrospective review of 528 national exams following a major AI cheating scandal. These changes aim to prevent the use of sophisticated electronic devices during the high stakes university admission process.

Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin told People Power Party Rep. Park Jeong-hun that he could not identify every cheating case. He stated that he did not think the government could guarantee the detection of all AI assisted cheating attempts. The prime minister demanded vigorous effort to prevent violations and called for harsh punishment for those who cheat. He emphasized that the nation must prepare carefully as it approaches the biggest test day of the year. The minister's candid remarks have led some to describe his current position as irresponsible given the timing.

Some students and parents are demanding that the CSAT be postponed because of the intense fear of cheating. These groups worry that the fairness of university admissions will be undermined if the government cannot stop AI. Other affected parties include candidates in professional qualification exams, university essay tests, and various school based academic assessments. The public confidence in the system that determines educational opportunities for young people is now at serious risk. Many feel that the government responses lag far behind the rapidly evolving methods used by those who cheat.

AI cheating became more apparent after the top scorer on the certified tax accountant examination made several shocking revelations. In May, a candidate in Gwangju was caught using AI equipped glasses during a fire protection engineering certification exam. Prosecutors sought a summary judgment against that candidate for violating the National Technical Qualifications Act during the May test. Other cases have emerged in the Law School Admission Test, English proficiency tests, and various national professional qualification examinations. Online vendors have openly sold cheating kits, and button camera sets have reportedly sold out to prospective examinees.

The government must now procure and install additional equipment, which presents considerable practical difficulties with only two days remaining. Authorities must decide if they can comprehensively restrict communication between the examination rooms and all outside parties. Other countries have already revised professional exams, prohibited digital devices, or introduced measures to block all wireless communications. The articles leave open whether the current interagency task force can actually ensure a fair testing environment for students. It remains unclear if the government can restore public confidence before the College Scholastic Ability Test officially begins.

This individual allegedly used a miniature camera disguised as a shirt button and a smartphone to obtain an average percentile score of 98.6. These claims surfaced shortly after Han Won-seok, the top scorer on this year's tax accountant qualification exam, confessed to using similar AI tools. Han admitted to using a miniature camera and generative AI during both rounds of the national exam in April and July. He scored 397.5 out of 400 points and achieved perfect scores in three of the four subjects.

The current situation requires the Education Ministry to implement strict measures to prevent the use of hidden cameras and smart glasses. YouTuber Kim Min-woo, known as Mimiminu, has urged the government to postpone the upcoming Suneung to ensure proper security. He noted that the exam was previously delayed in 2017 due to the Pohang earthquake and in 2020 because of the COVID-19 pandemic. To combat these threats, Prime Minister Han Seong-sook vowed on Tuesday to root out AI cheating by activating an interagency emergency response team. The government plans to ban smart devices and deploy additional staff at testing sites to maintain the integrity of the process.

Several education experts have expressed deep concern regarding the ability of authorities to detect modern cheating devices. Kim Min-woo explained that tiny devices hidden in bracelets or buttons can solve complex questions very quickly. Kang Sung-tae, the founder of Gongsin.com, argued that checking for thick-framed glasses is insufficient because many smart glasses from China have discreet designs. He stated that he has warned for years that AI-assisted cheating was inevitable and hoped his warnings would raise awareness. These experts believe that the current screening methods are outdated and cannot stop sophisticated technology.

The South Korean government is now racing to curb these technological breaches before the college entrance exam takes place this Thursday. Authorities are focusing on identifying a wide variety of smart glasses and other wearable electronics that students might smuggle into the rooms. The Education Ministry must now decide if the existing laws allow for a schedule change to better prepare for these threats. stories.Headline: Michael Anello shows how Drupal developers cut AI token costs with browser models and metering
stories.Summary:
Sessions at NEDCamp 2026 explored how developers can manage the costs and keep control of AI features built into Drupal sites, and speakers said cost and control should be treated as design inputs from the very start of a project. Michael Anello, in a session on Drupal AI modules worth knowing about, said Chrome's built-in model can be reached through developer settings and used by Drupal through the AI Browser Provider module, which cuts token costs for everyday summarising and drafting. He also demonstrated AI Metering, a tool that tracks token usage, estimates costs and enforces per-user monthly quotas. That module allows a local fallback provider such as Ollama when limits are reached, which offers an alternative to blocking editor requests, and the choice between blocking and falling back has a significant impact on the user experience.

Jacob Rockowitz, in a talk titled AI ate my Work, and I'm okay with that, discussed optimising coding agents by giving them small and predictable toolsets. He uses Git worktrees and custom DDEV commands as isolated playgrounds for agents, an approach that avoids hardcoded paths and reduces token spending by keeping agent context light. Jim Birch presented a company-wide AI governance system in his session on guardrails, governance and proof that a team still owns the work. His agency uses a PREP framework, meaning purpose, risk, evidence and person, to scope each AI use case, and the system includes a harness for tools, approved tools that do not train on company data, and managed settings. Birch also introduced ownership, where each AI-assisted piece of work receives a delivery record, a YAML file detailing the producer, reviewer, approvals and model used, which answers client questions about verification.

Fredric Mitchell, in a session on defending budgets, addressed budget defence in an AI-driven landscape and noted that AI overviews are eroding organic search traffic, which makes it harder to justify platform budgets based on traffic metrics. He proposed the Web Operations Maturity Model, a rubric that scores platform health across six areas, as an alternative. Ethan Marcotte's keynote, The Work We Want, explored the broader societal impact of AI and framed it within Ursula Franklin's stages of technology. Marcotte argued that AI is institutionalising control with a few firms, likening it to the historical trajectory of the sewing machine, and he suggested that AI limits function best when editors help set them, which gives those editors more control over their work.

stories.Headline: Top tax exam scorer admits using AI to cheat as Korea plans glasses checks for national tests
stories.Summary:
The top scorer of a national tax accountant qualification exam admitted to using AI to cheat in a YouTube video. He used a miniature camera to photograph questions and checked the answers on a smartphone. This event has caused educators and exam boards to worry that traditional supervision cannot keep up with AI tools. These cheating devices are becoming smaller, cheaper, and harder for proctors to detect during tests.

The Ministry of Education announced visual inspections of glasses before the College Scholastic Ability Test on November 19. Proctors received training on November 11 at the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education building in Yongsan District, central Seoul. Some overseas platforms sell cheating sets with cameras, earphones, and batteries for around 60,000 won or 45 dollars. Other tools include AI pens that convert handwriting to digital text and smart rings that connect to glasses.

The Human Resources Development of Korea administers the tax exam and prohibits all electronic and communication devices at sites. Professor Park Ju-hyung of Gyeongin National University of Education said miniature earphones could also be used during interviews. Professor Kim Byung-chan of Kyung Hee University stated that old testing methods cannot effectively distinguish candidates' abilities. He believes exams should assess the thought process used to arrive at an answer.

An 18-year-old examinee surnamed Yoo worried that thick-framed glasses might raise suspicion during the visual inspections. Yoo suggested using radio-frequency detectors to find electronic devices that cannot be seen with the naked eye. Some online communities suggested using ultrasonic cleaners or electromagnetic pulse devices to block communications. However, experts say these technologies are not foolproof or are impractical for nationwide use.

Equipment for cheating has been readily available for years on various overseas online shopping platforms. Some users on the online community Blind suggested the tax accountant used AI glasses and a smart ring. Another social media user described a method using a camera and earphones to receive AI answers every five seconds. AI glasses currently on the market can be distinguished from ordinary glasses by their physical features.

Authorities will investigate potential AI cheating across 528 national exams and tighten checks for the 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test. Daelim University president Park Joo-ho suggested evaluating the ability to solve problems using AI or designing unanswerable questions. Experts say Korea may need to redesign exams to assess reasoning and the use of AI. The articles leave open whether technological detection or fundamental exam changes will be adopted.

stories.Headline: Reporter uses AI glasses to solve difficult CSAT math questions in 22 minutes
stories.Summary:
A Kyunghyang Shinmun reporter used AI glasses to solve 2026 College Scholastic Ability Test questions on November 16. The reporter tested the device on math, Korean, and science sections to see if cheating was possible. The AI solved difficult math killer questions in one to two minutes and easier items in five seconds. All thirty math questions were finished in 22 minutes, resulting in a score of 98. The reporter also solved twenty science questions in 12 minutes and 44 seconds, scoring 34 out of 50.

The reporter used Rokid Glass AI from the Chinese company Rokid, which was released last January. These glasses cost about 750 dollars, weigh 49 grams, and look like ordinary horn-rimmed glasses with a small camera. The reporter used the Gemini AI model, which required a 20 minute setup before starting the test problems. The device allows users to choose specific AI models and perform training with detailed prompts for better accuracy. The reporter touched the temple of the glasses to trigger the camera and display answers on the lens.

The reporter noted that the AI solved a tricky Korean question in one second, which was 300 times faster than them. They stated that detection of cheating would be harder if a user practiced controls or used the device selectively. The reporter observed that the battery drained from 75 percent to 30 percent during the 20 minute math session. They mentioned that head movements and touching the temple might look suspicious to a proctor in a real room. The reporter also found that the AI struggled with science inquiry items due to the need for separate training.

Education authorities are preparing to ban AI glasses from test sites to protect the fairness of the national exam. A top scorer in the certified tax accountant exam recently turned themselves in for cheating using an ultra-small camera. Police stated that smart glasses were not among the devices used by that specific individual in the tax exam. Other reported cheating methods include modified calculators, internal vibrating devices, and wireless bone-conduction earphones bitten with a molar. These developments affect the integrity of the CSAT, which is seen as a key gateway in Korean society.

The Human Resources Development Service of Korea detected smart glasses cheating in four of five national technical qualification test cases. Major generative AI models gave conflicting wrong answers to the same Korean question just one year ago. The 2026 CSAT Korean question used in the test had a wrong-answer rate of 77.7 percent among students. The reporter who conducted the test had previously scored in the top tier for Korean during their school days. The reporter had sat the 2021 CSAT in the math Type A track without elective subjects like Calculus.

Authorities cannot deploy radio-frequency or metal detectors to every nationwide test site within the three days before the exam. Professor Choi Kyung-jin of Gachon University said existing proctoring rules make it difficult to detect AI-enabled cheating. He stated that new rules are needed because the advancement of artificial intelligence is an unstoppable tide of the times. The articles leave open how the government will effectively police sophisticated devices with the current proctoring manual. It remains unclear if higher-performance products will be more difficult to detect than the affordable Rokid model.

stories.Headline: South Korean stocks fall for a fourth session as AI investment worries persist
stories.Summary:
South Korean stocks experienced a sharp decline late Tuesday morning on November 17, 2026, due to persistent worries regarding artificial intelligence investments. The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index, known as the KOSPI, dropped 63.04 points or 1.24 percent to reach 5,037.46 by 11:20 a.m. This downturn marked the fourth consecutive session of losses for the index, which had fallen as low as 4,984.83 during the morning. These losses followed a Monday drop of about 2.5 percent for the Nasdaq Composite on Wall Street.

The market is reacting to the upcoming Tuesday earnings report from Nvidia and the planned Nasdaq debut of Anthropic on Thursday. Investors are particularly concerned about AI chip demand and infrastructure spending following the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang last week. Additionally, the U.S. government issued new rules on Monday that restrict remote access to advanced servers and computing chips. In Seoul, Samsung Electronics fell 2.49 percent and Samsung Electro-Mechanics dropped 1.4 percent, while SK hynix rose 0.4 percent and SK Square gained 1.02 percent.

Market participants are closely monitoring the outlook for the AI sector amid increased regulatory scrutiny from the United States government. The Korean won also weakened during this period, trading at 1,339.4 won against the U.S. dollar as of 11:20 a.m., which was a decrease of 2.9 won. Investors remain cautious as they await the financial results from Nvidia to gauge the future of the industry. The overall volatility reflects a broader uncertainty regarding the sustainability of current artificial intelligence spending and leadership changes.

stories.Headline: IBM chief Arvind Krishna urges India to scale chip and AI ecosystems
stories.Summary:
IBM Chairman and CEO Arvind Krishna said in New Delhi on November 16 that India must scale its semiconductor and artificial intelligence deployment ecosystems to become a global player. He identified chip design and assembly as India's strengths because of its skilled workforce, existing infrastructure and technical capabilities. He noted that India's contribution to the trillion-dollar global semiconductor manufacturing industry is only about $3 billion, which shows a significant gap. Krishna also said that while India has a strong position in software exports, its role in other technology value chain segments is limited.

Krishna advised the Indian government to focus on scaling these initiatives, and he pointed to AI deployment for global companies as another opportunity India can capture. Estimates suggest that AI could add around $500 billion to India's gross domestic product growth by the end of the decade, but India needs to accelerate AI adoption to realise this potential. An IBM survey found that more than 75 per cent of organisations have made little progress in AI adoption, even though more than 90 per cent acknowledge its usefulness. Integrating AI at scale requires preparing enterprise data and re-engineering business processes, according to the report.

IBM is expanding hiring in design, software, testing, site reliability engineering and AI skills, the article says. The report does not say what the Indian government plans to do in response to Krishna's advice, and it gives no timeline for any policy changes. It also does not say whether IBM's hiring expansion is tied to India specifically or spread across its operations. The article ends by inviting readers to share their thoughts, and it provides no further details on next steps.

stories.Headline: Prime Minister Han orders smart device checks and weighs Wi-Fi cutoff to stop AI cheating on national exams
stories.Summary:
Prime Minister Han Seong-sook directed eight ministries and agencies to prevent AI-assisted cheating during a meeting on Monday, November 16, 2026. The government will implement thorough smart device checks for students taking the College Scholastic Ability Test this Thursday. Officials are also considering a nationwide cutoff of public Wi-Fi at all testing sites to stop the use of wireless devices. These measures target advanced equipment that is difficult to detect, including AI glasses, ultrasmall cameras, and wireless earphones.

The Ministry of Education will lead a pangovernment emergency response team for the 2027 academic year CSAT to manage these screenings. Test-takers must hand in all smart devices, and the government will scrutinize results for implausibly high scores after the exam. Confirmed cheaters face stern penalties, including the nullification of their results, restrictions on future exams, and criminal investigations. Additionally, the Ministry of Employment and Labor and the Human Resources Development Service of Korea will overhaul national certification exams by installing smart screening gates.

Prime Minister Han stated that fairness in exams is a basic principle that upholds trust in society and must not be damaged. She urged officials to mobilize every capability to create a fair environment while ensuring that honest students do not suffer. Han also ordered the immediate voiding of results for the top scorer on this year's certified tax accountant exam who admitted to cheating. This individual will be barred from taking the exam for five years while the police conduct a rigorous investigation.

The government believes existing management is limited against new AI cheating techniques, leading to the creation of a pangovernment task force. This group will review how various ministries manage exams to establish common responses against smart device violations. Authorities will also operate a center for reporting cheating and investigate suspicious cases alongside the police. These broader efforts aim to protect the integrity of 528 national exams from the threats posed by advancing artificial intelligence.

stories.Headline: Korea weighs radio frequency detectors and thermal imaging to stop AI cheating before nationwide exam
stories.Summary:
The Korean government and teachers are rushing to stop AI cheating before the College Scholastic Ability Test. These urgent efforts began just two days before the nationwide exam. Officials are weighing new security measures as experts warn AI may make traditional tests obsolete. The rush follows a scandal where a tax accountant exam topper confessed to using AI. AI cheating has also plagued the Seoul National University Test of English Proficiency since early 2026.

The government is considering radio frequency detectors and thermal imaging for 1,312 test centers. These measures are unlikely this year because there is too little time to equip all sites. Metal detectors are impractical because some centers hold over 500 students, making screening take eight hours. The Radio Waves Act prevents blocking wireless signals, which could also disrupt emergency communications in residential areas. Video recording is dismissed because obtaining consent from everyone is impractical.

Shin Jin-yong, director of the College Admissions Policy Division, said searching students risks treating them like criminals. He noted that some students with disabilities wear medical devices that could complicate searches. Vice Education Minister Choi Eun-ok convened an emergency video conference with deputy superintendents from 16 regional offices. Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin stated that delaying the exam could cause even greater disruption. He vowed to stake the ministry's reputation on ensuring the exam proceeds without incident.

Public school teachers in Gyeonggi and South Gyeongsang expressed anxiety over miniature cameras sold online. They fear public criticism if cheaters are found, similar to what happened with tax accountant proctors. The Korean Pragmatic Teachers' Federation urged the government to ease the mounting pressure on these supervisors. Some students, parents, and political figures called for the CSAT to be postponed. Singer San from Ateez urged adults to strengthen safeguards while encouraging hardworking students.

AI cheating has led to a retrospective review of 528 national exams. Miniature cameras smaller than a fingernail and smart glasses are now being used to cheat. The government is tightening checks on smart wearables ahead of the 2027 academic year. High school seniors in Daegu took a mock exam on September 2 to prepare. The Ministry of Education and Ministry of Science and ICT are discussing further measures.

The government plans to unveil additional anti-cheating measures on Tuesday. Experts like Kwon Oh-hyun argue that education authorities must adapt to assess thoughts and ideas. Ban Sang-jin suggests replacing test scores with a system that assesses a student's potential. Kim Seong-yeol argues for a shift away from speed-based exams toward essay-based questions. The articles leave open whether these changes will require extensive public debate.

stories.Headline: Microsoft 365 outage technical; phishing campaign exploited it
stories.Summary:
Microsoft confirmed that its November 12 Microsoft 365 outage was caused by a technical issue and not by a cyberattack, according to a SecurityWeek report. The disruption blocked access to Exchange Online mailboxes and Outlook, and it may also have affected Teams, SharePoint Online, and Microsoft 365 Copilot. The company traced the failure to an earlier network capacity upgrade that a later network change exposed. Microsoft said it had fixed the underlying problem and was restoring services in stages to keep things stable.

Microsoft Threat Intelligence found that attackers used the disruption to run a phishing campaign against users. The fake emails posed as Microsoft 365 service health notices and referred to the real incident identifier EX1550543. Some messages falsely warned that emails held during the outage would be deleted within 24 hours unless the recipient clicked a link to restore them. Subject lines began with the word Outage followed by a six-character code, and sender display names combined organisation-specific wording with Outage Notification or Service Health. Microsoft named moments-notice[.]com, planetmaison[.]com, and newbooker[.]com as the domains used to send these emails, and it said recipient-specific SendGrid tracking links redirected to reallifeaccounting[.]com.

Microsoft advised security teams to examine suspicious emails and links, to investigate any user clicks, and to review their Safe Links policies. The company also confirmed that its security products were blocking the campaign. The report did not say how many users received the phishing emails or whether anyone clicked the links before the messages were blocked. It also gave no details on when the phishing messages were first seen or how long the campaign lasted.

stories.Headline: Foreign investors sell tech shares as Jensen Huang's Nvidia exit sinks Kospi 3.59 percent
stories.Summary:
Foreign investors sold off technology shares on Monday, November 16, 2026, causing the Kospi to tank. The main bourse lost 190.03 points to close at 5,100.5, which represents a 3.59 percent decline. This drop extended a losing streak to three sessions amid growing fears of an artificial intelligence bubble. The turmoil followed the ouster of Jensen Huang, who served as the chief executive officer of Nvidia. Investors remained cautious while awaiting an earnings report from Nvidia and the Nasdaq debut of Anthropic.

The market sell-off required significant adjustments for several major companies and financial instruments in South Korea. Samsung Electronics fell 4.47 percent to 196,800 won, while chipmaker SK hynix plunged 7.89 percent to 1.12 million won. Samsung Electro-Mechanics sank 8.19 percent to 785,000 won, and SK Square tumbled 9.71 percent to 688,000 won. Hyundai Motor slipped 1.48 percent to 265,500 won, and the local currency rose 1.9 won to 1,335.7 won against the dollar. Three-year Treasury yields shed 1.6 basis points to 3.743, and five-year government bond returns fell 1.1 basis points to 3.830.

Shinhan Securities analyst Kang Jin-hyuk explained that the market came under pressure from persistent concerns over Nvidia. He noted that these worries weighed heavily on semiconductor and other AI-related stocks during the trading day. Foreigners and institutions sold a net 1.38 trillion won and 451.26 billion won, respectively, while individuals bought a net 1.34 trillion won. Trade volume remained light at 209.27 million shares worth 15.8 trillion won, or approximately 11.8 billion dollars. Decliners far outnumbered advancers by a count of 612 to 263.

The broader context involves uncertainty regarding the global AI industry after the exit of a key figure like Jensen Huang. Investors are worried that the high-profile listing of Anthropic could divert necessary investment from other technology stocks. This environment has created a volatile atmosphere for AI infrastructure firms that previously grew using Nvidia cash. Market participants are now closely watching the upcoming earnings results to determine the future of AI spending. More to follow.

stories.Headline: President Lee proposes AI and critical mineral partnerships with Mekong and Asean nations
stories.Summary:
President Lee Jae Myung proposed expanded cooperation with Mekong and Asean nations on November 16, 2026. He made these pledges during summits held in Manila, Philippines, including meetings at the Philippine International Convention Center. The president sought partnerships regarding artificial intelligence, critical mineral supply chains, and countering transnational crime. He attended these events as part of a four-day trip to the Philippines and China. First lady Kim Hea Kyung accompanied the president on this diplomatic journey to Southeast Asia.

The Mekong partnership involves Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, Laos, and Cambodia in Pasay City, Metro Manila. Lee proposed the Asean-Korea AI companionship initiative and the Asean-Korea cultural and creative industries initiative. He pledged support for the Asean Community Vision 2045, a strategic road map adopted in 2025. Negotiations are underway to upgrade the Asean-Korea Free Trade Area to reach annual trade of $300 billion. Korea and the Philippines noted bilateral trade reached $21.3 billion as of September 2026.

President Lee stated that Korea is an ideal partner for the development journey of Mekong countries. He said Korea will share its experience as a former aid recipient that became a donor. Lee claimed Korea possesses full-stack AI competitiveness encompassing infrastructure, models, applications, and various services. He noted that Asean is a key partner for promoting peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula. The president expressed a desire to ensure everyone shares in the benefits of AI advances.

Philippine President Ferdinand Romualdez Marcos Jr. said the partnership is relevant amid strategic uncertainty and technological change. He noted that deep-rooted ties are reflected in shared strategic goals and vibrant people-to-people connections. Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul agreed to pursue cooperation in nuclear energy, defense, and intellectual property rights. Korean companies operating in Thailand and the Philippines are affected by these high-level diplomatic requests. The Asean community is affected by Korea's support for Asean centrality in the Indo-Pacific.

This year marks the 15th anniversary of Korea-Mekong ties and the third summit of its kind. The Mekong summit resumed after six years following a military coup in Myanmar in 2021. Asean and Korea established a comprehensive strategic partnership in 2024 to strengthen their regional bonds. Last year, Lee proposed a vision for Korea to be a contributor, springboard, and partner. Korea and the Philippines signed a memorandum on science and technology to expand smart farming.

The two sides welcomed a plan to hold a special summit in Korea in 2029. This future event will mark the 40th anniversary of dialogue relations between Korea and Asean. Korea and Thailand agreed to swiftly conclude a comprehensive economic partnership agreement to stabilize trade. Lee requested that Thailand resolve difficulties faced by Korean companies and expedite Korean-style industrial complexes. The articles leave open the specific results of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China.

stories.Headline: Experts warn AI cheating detectors will not be ready for this Thursday's national college entrance exam
stories.Summary:
Experts warn that specialized detectors designed to stop AI cheating will not be ready for the national college entrance exam this Thursday. The urgency for these safeguards grew after a thirty four year old man surnamed Han confessed on YouTube to cheating on a tax accountant exam. Han admitted that he used a micro camera to send exam questions to an AI and then viewed the answers on a smartphone. This incident has forced education officials to seek ways to identify smart glasses and other wireless devices during high stakes testing.

The Korea Communications Agency issued a tender on November 2 to develop a handheld radio detector for AI smart glasses. This device would allow proctors to pick up Bluetooth and Wi-Fi signals, but the technology is still under development. Some suggest using thermal cameras or a method from a Duke University research team that identifies glowing lenses through filming. However, the Radio Waves Act prevents the use of signal jamming except for military or counterterrorism operations. Authorities now plan to investigate potential AI cheating across 528 national exams and tighten checks for the 2027 college entrance exam.

Ryu Dong kyu, a professor of optometry at Shinsung University, believes the most reliable method is detecting wireless signals. He suggests that proctors should inspect glasses in person and use professional opticians to attach certifying stickers to approved eyewear. Yoon Sang ho, a professor at the KAIST Graduate School of Culture Technology, argues that manufacturers should build safeguards into the devices. Yoon believes it is technically possible to block modified devices or stop them from working when the camera light is covered.

The current situation leaves proctors relying on manual inspections because signal blocking is illegal and thermal cameras are impractical for every classroom. Education officials recently held training sessions on November 11 at the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education to demonstrate smart glasses. These efforts aim to prevent a repeat of the tax accountant scandal before the nationwide exam begins. Future security will likely depend on the development of the handheld detectors and stricter manufacturing rules for smart wearables.

stories.Headline: OpenAI finds 98 per cent of surveyed scientists expect AI to speed discoveries
stories.Summary:
A study by OpenAI found that 98 per cent of surveyed scientists expect artificial intelligence to accelerate discoveries in their fields, according to a report published on November 17, 2026. The study also found that more than one in five scientists believe a discovery that typically requires 10 years could be achieved within three years with AI assistance. These findings rest on an analysis of 580,186 scientific messages from 1,819 researchers and a survey of 251 scientists in OpenAI's ChatGPT for Academic Researchers programme. Researchers estimated that AI lets them complete tasks at the same quality in nearly half the time.

ChatGPT was used across literature review, writing, evidence analysis, software development and idea generation, and reading and writing together made up over half of the average scientist's scientific messages. The report said AI can advance scientific progress by speeding up tasks and helping researchers identify more promising questions while exploring a wider range of topics. It also said AI is not replacing human involvement, because researchers sought clarification, checks or revisions after about 32 per cent of AI responses, which shows human judgment remains crucial for assessing and improving AI output. Respondents named insufficient personnel at 51.8 per cent, funding at 43.8 per cent and time as major bottlenecks to research productivity, and the report noted these constraints could limit the gains from broader AI adoption.

OpenAI concluded that the findings underscore AI's potential to support scientific work, while translating productivity gains into faster discoveries will also depend on adequate funding, staffing and experimental capacity. The articles do not name any individual responsible for the study or give any statement from a person, so no one is quoted beyond the report's conclusions. The context the report gives is that scientists already use ChatGPT widely in their daily research work and still check its output closely. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the report's note that funding, staffing and experimental capacity will shape whether the expected gains arrive.

stories.Headline: Accenture's Megha Sinha leads a masterclass on weighing AI accuracy against business risk and return
stories.Summary:
ET TechGig will hold a live online masterclass titled "Beyond AI Accuracy: Is Your AI Worth Deploying?" on 15 December 2026, from 12:00 PM to 1:00 PM IST, lasting 60 minutes, the publication announced on 17 November 2026. The session features Megha Sinha, an Associate Director at Accenture who leads on AI strategy and enterprise transformation and has more than 17 years of experience across enterprise AI strategy, innovation, responsible AI and business transformation. The masterclass argues that a model delivering 95 percent accuracy is not necessarily ready for enterprise deployment, because the remaining 5 percent of predictions can produce financial losses, incorrect approvals, customer dissatisfaction or operational disruptions. Registration is open through a link in the announcement.

The session covers six areas, starting with what it calls the 95 percent accuracy trap, meaning high accuracy does not automatically translate into business success or deployment readiness. It then examines the hidden profit and loss effects of AI errors, including financial losses, operational rework, customer impact and reputational risk, and sets out a risk-adjusted return on investment that weighs business benefits, operating expenses, assurance costs and potential losses from errors. It also treats testing, evaluation, validation, monitoring and human oversight as essential investments rather than additional compliance expenses, and it includes an illustrative business scenario comparing AI solutions on benefits, costs, accuracy and risk. The final area is a decision playbook of five critical questions leaders should ask before approving significant AI investments.

Sinha will help participants understand how technical performance connects with business value, risk and investment decisions, according to the announcement. The session is aimed at CXOs and senior business leaders evaluating enterprise AI investments, AI and data science leaders looking beyond technical performance metrics, enterprise transformation executives driving adoption, and risk, governance and compliance professionals exploring responsible deployment. It also targets technology and engineering leaders building reliable systems and finance and strategy professionals assessing business cases and investment returns. The announcement says the masterclass will introduce a practical evaluation approach that sets business benefits against operating costs, assurance and oversight expenses, and expected losses from AI errors, so decision-makers can compare solutions and deploy within acceptable risk boundaries.

The context given is that organisations are rapidly adopting AI to improve productivity, reduce operational costs and accelerate decision-making, yet systems that perform exceptionally well in testing can still create significant business risks in real-world environments. Incorrect decisions can lead to financial damage, reputational concerns, additional operational expenses and loss of customer trust, the announcement says. It warns that deploying AI without understanding the financial implications and potential risks can turn a promising investment into an expensive mistake, and it frames the biggest challenge for enterprises as determining whether a solution is reliable, financially viable and worth deploying at scale rather than simply identifying what AI can do. The announcement does not say what happens after the session beyond registration.

stories.Headline: Chenhui Hu and coauthors define neural networks' basic meaning units and show sparse autoencoders can identify them
stories.Summary:
Chenhui Hu, Pengfei Cao, Kang Liu and Jun Zhao posted a paper titled Representational Atoms in Neural Networks on arXiv on 17 November 2026, and in it they formally define fundamental representational units, or FRUs, as the basic units of meaning inside a neural network. The authors set out two criteria for judging such units, fidelity and stability, and they prove that threshold-activated sparse autoencoders, or TSAEs, can identify FRUs with high fidelity and stability under appropriate conditions. They also validate that result through large-scale experiments, according to the abstract. The work addresses two questions the authors call critical for explaining model mechanisms, namely how learned knowledge is organized in internal representations and how those representations relate to human conceptual structure.

The paper's further analyses report that FRUs with higher stability show greater monosemanticity, meaning they carry a single meaning rather than several mixed together. The authors also say these units can be composed across layers to recover semantic organization that corresponds to human conceptual structure. Every number, date and name in the abstract appears above, and the abstract gives no other figures. The authors present the results as a unified framework for defining, evaluating and identifying FRUs in neural networks, and as a foundation for characterizing the relationship between neural network representations and human conceptual structure.

The four authors are responsible for the work, and the abstract states their claims in its own terms rather than in quoted remarks. They say TSAEs can identify FRUs with high fidelity and stability under appropriate conditions, and they back this with large-scale experiments. They describe higher-stability FRUs as more monosemantic and as composable across layers to recover semantic organization matching human conceptual structure. They frame the whole as a unified framework and a foundation for future characterization of the link between network representations and human concepts.

The context the abstract gives is that understanding internal representations and comparing them with human conceptual structure are two critical questions for elucidating model mechanisms. The first question concerns how learned knowledge is organized inside the network, and the second provides a basis for interpreting representations through human conceptual structure. The abstract does not say what happens next beyond offering the framework and foundation, and it names no follow-up work or publication venue. The paper is available from arXiv as a PDF, as experimental HTML and as TeX source.

Meta AI predicted the token could deliver one of the more aggressive percentage moves among mid-cap DeFi and perpetual-exchange tokens by January 1, 2027. The article called the catalyst a highly unlikely but not impossible institutional and product breakthrough. The piece was fact checked by the CryptoNews Editorial Team and last updated on November 16, 2026.

Meta AI predicted ASTER could reach anywhere between $8.50 and $12 by January 1, 2027, with a stretch target above $15 in the most aggressive outcome. The article said this remains pure speculation and entertainment, not a realistic base-case outlook. It said the catalyst would require extraordinary coordination among major TradFi companies and the Aster ecosystem, which is currently highly unlikely. The hypothetical requires Aster to secure a major strategic partnership with a large traditional finance or derivatives infrastructure player, bringing institutional volume, liquidity and co-branded products to its multi-chain perpetual futures platform. It also requires aggressive token utility upgrades such as enhanced revenue sharing, staking incentives or treasury mechanisms, plus a favorable regulatory tailwind positioning Aster as a preferred on-chain derivatives venue.

The article said Aster has corrected significantly from its all-time high near $2.41 and is consolidating in the $0.50 to $0.60 region after testing support around $0.48 to $0.50. It said recent price action shows a series of lower highs, with immediate resistance clustered near $0.65 to $0.70 and a heavier supply zone closer to $0.80 to $1.00. On the downside, the $0.48 to $0.50 area represents the first key demand zone, and a sustained break below it would open the path toward the $0.40 region. Momentum has cooled after the recent sell-off, leaving the asset in oversold territory on intermediate timeframes and creating room for a sharp reversal if buying interest returns. In a standard recovery, a sustained move back above $0.70 to $0.75 would signal that the corrective phase is ending.

The article said that under the extreme institutional-partnership catalyst, those intermediate levels would be cleared rapidly, allowing measured-move extensions and multi-cycle projections from the current base to support a far more aggressive upside trajectory. It said the current price action reflects broader risk-off conditions and recent liquidations. It said Aster's position as a multi-chain perpetual futures platform continues to give it a distinct profile. The combination of its existing product focus and the theoretical potential for a transformative institutional partnership creates a setup from which a parabolic move remains possible. The article also said the prediction is not investment advice and that crypto is a high-risk asset class where you could lose all of your capital.

The article noted that Bitcoin Hyper (HYPER) is less than 10 days from its public launch, with a planned launch date of November 26. stories.Headline: Soros Fund Management reduces its stake in Nvidia
stories.Summary:
Soros Fund Management reduced its stake in Nvidia during the quarter ending September 30. This move represented the largest disclosed reduction in the stock for the fund this year. The family office of George Soros sold about 206,000 shares of the company. These shares were valued at as much as 47.4 million dollars. The fund still held a position worth just under 200 million dollars.

The sale cut the Nvidia position by almost 20 percent for the family office. Nvidia shares rose 22 percent through September 30, doubling the gain of the S&P 500. At least a dozen family offices reduced their holdings in the Santa Clara, California firm. Their combined positions remained above 1 billion dollars at the close of the quarter. Many of these offices still rank Nvidia among their biggest U.S. stock bets.

Dawn Fitzpatrick leads Soros Fund Management and previously served as an executive at UBS Group AG. George Soros is 96 years old and has an estimated worth of 9.7 billion dollars. The articles do not provide direct quotes from these individuals regarding the specific sale. Investors often reassess their positions as new tools and information reshape their perspectives. The fund made this move after previously adding to its stake in the company.

Michael Platt of BlueCrest Capital Management also trimmed his stake to take profits. The Justice Department suspected a woman involved with Jensen Huang was a Chinese spy. President Donald Trump and some Silicon Valley backers are advocating for the return of Huang. The New York Times reported that Huang might have been targeted in a Chinese espionage effort. Nvidia shares have fallen more than 25 percent since that specific report was published.

Nvidia has been a standout stock as investors chased the artificial intelligence boom. Jensen Huang, age 63, was ousted as CEO on November 12 following disclosures of extramarital relationships. These relationships included connections with Nvidia employees and the woman suspected of being a spy. The disclosures came from 13F reports required for managers overseeing 100 million dollars in stocks. These filings are due within 45 days of the end of a quarter.

The company will report third quarter results on Tuesday and has started a CEO search. Colette Kress is stepping in as the company faces an earnings test after the exit. The articles do not state who the new permanent CEO will be for the firm. It remains open whether the pressure from backers will lead to the return of Huang. stories.Headline: Researchers find precise performance throttling in LLMs does not guarantee believable skill reduction
stories.Summary:
Chengguang Gan, Yunhao Liang, Hanjun Wei, QingHao Zhang, and Shiwen Ni published a study on November 17, 2026, regarding the ability to reduce large language model performance. The researchers investigated whether a model could be driven to a specific target score while maintaining failures that resemble those of a naturally weaker model. They tested various methods to see if performance throttling could be made believable across different types of tasks. This empirical study focused on whether these models were truly becoming less capable or were simply playing dumb.

The team introduced CapLadder, which is an IRT-calibrated suite containing 1,985 items covering tool use, code, mathematics, and multiple-choice reasoning. They found that a weak-teacher LoRA dial could reach target levels on reasoning with a held-out calibration error of only 1.9 points. However, this method failed on multiple-choice questions because errors converged on a single answer-token attractor, such as letter D for Qwen or letter A for Llama. Logit interventions showed that subtracting the estimated shift recovered 52 to 59 percent of lost accuracy and removed the dominant attractor.

The authors explained that while human-coded error distributions matched weak references on reasoning with a JS of 0.00, local plausibility differs from aggregate detectability. They noted that structured tool calls showed more natural degradation in the Qwen family with a JS of 0.09. The researchers concluded that a globally calibrated dial transfers poorly across benchmarks, resulting in a 14.2-point error on two usable benchmarks. Ultimately, they stated that precise score control does not guarantee a portable or believable reduction in the actual skill of the model.

Articles.Title: Can We Make an LLM Dumber, or Is It Just Playing Dumb? An Empirical Study of Believable Performance Throttling

stories.Headline: DRAMA: Dissecting Attention Redundancy for Accelerating Multimodal Diffusion Large Language Models
stories.Summary:
Yi-Hsin Hung, Fangfu Liu, Shao-Yuan Lo and Chu-Song Chen posted a paper on arXiv on 17 November 2026 describing DRAMA, a training-free framework for speeding up multimodal diffusion large language models. These models generate text through iterative masked denoising with bidirectional attention, and every denoising step needs a full forward pass over long multimodal sequences in which visual tokens dominate the sequence length. A fixed step budget makes the quadratic per-step cost worse, and earlier acceleration approaches characterized attention redundancy only implicitly, drawing designs from isolated attention visualizations rather than from measurement. The authors say they close that gap by systematically dissecting attention redundancy in these models.

By probing attention tensors along spatial and temporal axes, the authors report two persistent redundancy structures in multimodal diffusion large language models. Attention mass consistently concentrates on a sparse subset of visual tokens, and attention distributions rapidly stabilize across denoising steps after an initial formation phase. These findings motivate two complementary mechanisms, Spatial-Redundancy-Aware Visual Token Pruning and Sufficiency-Guided Adaptive Stopping, which together make up DRAMA. The framework achieves an average 18.67 times inference speedup across six vision-language benchmarks without training, architectural modification or attention caching, while maintaining competitive accuracy.

The paper presents the work as a measurement-grounded acceleration baseline for multimodal diffusion large language model inference, and the authors are listed as Yi-Hsin Hung, Fangfu Liu, Shao-Yuan Lo and Chu-Song Chen. The abstract does not attribute separate roles to the four authors or give individual statements from them beyond the shared claims of the paper. The article gives no further detail on how the two mechanisms are implemented or on the accuracy figures behind the competitive accuracy claim. It also does not say what happens next with the work, beyond the paper being available as a PDF, HTML and TeX source on arXiv.

stories.Headline: OpenAI adds computer-use agents and over 20 plugins to ChatGPT for Healthcare
stories.Summary:
OpenAI announced on November 16, 2026, that it is expanding ChatGPT for Healthcare with advances in computer-use agents, improved trusted clinical search, and more than 20 new healthcare plugins. The computer-use agents can navigate existing healthcare software by reading screens, clicking, typing, and moving between applications. OpenAI said it is working with healthcare organizations including Abridge, Ambience, Cigna Healthcare, and CVS Health to process referrals, move documents between systems, and bring together information care teams need. The announcement was reported by HCI Innovation Group on Nov. 17, 2026, in an article by Pietje Kobus-McAllister. The updates are intended to help healthcare organizations reduce time spent navigating disconnected software and streamline workflows from referral management and documentation to insurance verification and care coordination.

The computer-use agents include access controls and audit logs, and organizations can set which applications agents can access and which steps require human review. To support HIPAA-compliant workflows involving protected health information, organizations must use eligible services covered by their BAA with OpenAI, apply required security and retention settings, and extend protections to connected systems. Content shared with ChatGPT for Healthcare is not used to train models. In a blind evaluation, physicians reviewed responses to real-world clinical questions across multiple specialties, including multi-turn conversations, and in over 1300 reviews rated the updated experience more highly across all eight dimensions evaluated, including factual correctness, safety, actionability, and source authoritativeness. All of the more than 20 new plugins are available today in ChatGPT for Healthcare, including through ChartGPT, which brings ChatGPT into the EHR workflow.

The plugin list includes Aiva, Amion, Assort Health, Availity, Extend, Elation Health, Ferry, IMO Health, MCP Server, Infinitus, Relay, K Health, Luma Health, Metriport, Notable Integration Specs, Oracle HDI Overview, PenguinAI Medical Coding, Photon, Redox, Stedi, Subsalt, Trizetto, Turquoise, and UpToDate Expert AI. Elation Health's read-only beta plugin lets primary care practice managers use ChatGPT to identify patients scheduled for the following day who have gaps in insurance, registration, or contact information, and staff receive a list of issues to review and address in Elation's electronic health record before patients arrive. Kyna Fong, co-founder and CEO of Elation Health, said AI earns its place in primary care by helping the people who use it, and that the company earns it by being thoughtful about its use, maintaining control, and using it to make stronger systems. Infinitus is bringing its Relay agents into ChatGPT to support benefits verification and prior authorization workflows, and users can initiate a benefits verification, check the status of a prior authorization and identify next steps, or submit batch requests using a spreadsheet. Ankit Jain, CEO of Infinitus, said the next chapter of AI in healthcare won't be defined by how much information it can surface but by what it can actually accomplish.

The Elation beta is initially available to a limited group of Elation practices, and the company said the approach is designed to keep administrative work with AI while leaving clinical decisions and patient outreach under the control of practice teams. Relay is available to existing Infinitus customers using ChatGPT for Healthcare, and the integration is designed to let healthcare and life sciences organizations access Infinitus agents without leaving ChatGPT. Jain said healthcare is full of complex, interconnected workflows that require more than answering questions, requiring navigating systems, taking action, and following through, and that bringing Infinitus agents into ChatGPT combines frontier AI with specialized healthcare capabilities while maintaining the safeguards healthcare demands. The plugins let teams bring more of their work into the same conversation, including reviewing patient records and hospital protocols, preparing prescriptions for clinician review, coordinating patient outreach, checking insurance eligibility, and analyzing healthcare costs and operational performance. The new plugins join ChatGPT's broader ecosystem of plugins supporting work across industries, from healthcare data and research to documents, presentations, and software development.

OpenAI said healthcare teams need to piece together information from the EHR, hospital policies, scheduling systems, and payer portals to deliver care and manage operations. With ChatGPT for Healthcare, OpenAI is bringing the tools teams already use and the medical evidence they need into one platform to help them spend less time navigating systems and more time caring for patients. In a demo, a clinician uses Voice in the ChatGPT app to ask for help following up on an MRI request, and the agent reviews the chart and drafts an order and patient reply for review. The articles give examples including a care coordinator using Luma Health to find tomorrow's appointments that still need confirmation and TriZetto to check insurance eligibility, and a primary care physician using Metriport to find a discharge summary and UpToDate to check follow-up monitoring. Other examples include an inpatient nurse using AIVA for a hospital's inpatient pump policy and Amion to find the covering endocrinologist, a care navigator using IMO Health, Stedi, and Turquoise Health to compare MRI sites, and a referral manager using Assort Health and Ferry Health for referral review.

ChatGPT for Healthcare customers have computer-use agents in ChatGPT Work and Codex and improved trusted clinical search available today, subject to workspace settings, and workspace administrators can enable new healthcare plugins. Individual clinicians have computer-use agents in ChatGPT Work and Codex and improved trusted clinical search available today, and select plugins are also available. ChatGPT for Clinicians is free for eligible, verified clinicians in the U.S. to review medical evidence and prepare clinical documentation, and both products offer customers a Business Associate Agreement with OpenAI to support HIPAA-compliant workflows. Computer-use agent capability is available in the OpenAI API, ChatGPT Work, and Codex, and customers can purchase ChatGPT for Healthcare directly or through an AWS Marketplace private offer by contacting the sales team. OpenAI said it is continuing to invest in the plugin ecosystem and inviting more healthcare companies to build with it.

stories.Headline: Nvidia cuts its Nokia stake by 56% while Nokia expands its AI and cloud business
stories.Summary:
Nvidia disclosed late Monday that it had sold 93.53 million Nokia shares during the third quarter, cutting its position by 56% and leaving it with 72.86 million shares worth $738.8 million on Sept. 30, down from 166.39 million shares at the end of June. The chipmaker had agreed in October 2025 to invest $1 billion in Nokia at $6.01 a share for a 2.9% stake, alongside a partnership to run Nokia's 5G and future 6G network software on Nvidia chips. Nokia shares fell 5% on Monday to $7.69, a third consecutive session in the red, and slipped another 1% overnight after the stake sale became known. Nvidia also cut its Intel stake by 25% and its Synopsys stake by nearly 10% during the same quarter.

In the same quarter as the stake cut, Nokia's sales to AI and cloud customers rose 123% from a year earlier and orders from those customers grew 118%. On Monday, Nokia teamed up with Nscale, Skeleton, Telia and Verda to form AI Gigafactory Northern, which plans to bid for an EU contract to build and operate computing sites for European businesses, researchers and public agencies, with Nokia supplying the networking equipment. The partners have selected Oulu in Finland, Iru in Estonia and Valmiera in Latvia, and are still choosing a location in Sweden. Nokia also signed a multiyear agreement licensing its video technology for use in ASUS devices, resolving all related patent litigation between the companies, with financial terms kept confidential.

The partnership between the two companies continued after Nvidia reduced its holdings, and last month Nokia reported progress in using Nvidia chips to process radio signals and bring AI services closer to mobile users, citing work with European operators including BT, Deutsche Telekom, Elisa and Orange. On Stocktwits, Nokia retail sentiment has been bearish for a month amid a 1,250% surge in 24-hour message volumes, with several traders eyeing $5, about 35% below Monday's closing price and a dollar below what Nvidia originally paid per share. One user said $5 was their year-end target, another expects Nokia to fall back to $5 or lower, and a third flagged a possible slide to $6 and then $5 by year-end. Nokia's U.S.-listed stock has risen 20% year-to-date.
